/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — cover system on a basis (01EO conditions 1–2) -/

/-- A **covering datum** on `X`: an index family of opens (the covered open is `⨆ i, c.2 i`).
Project-local: the lightweight cover representation matching the cover-local Čech lemmas
(`cechCohomology`, `faceShortComplex`), which are indexed by a family `ι → Opens X`. -/
abbrev CovDatum (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type (u + 1) :=
  Σ ι : Type u, ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X

/-- **Cover system on a basis** (Stacks 01EO conditions (1)–(2)). Records a basis `B`, a set of
admissible coverings `Cov`, the faces-in-basis datum (every finite intersection of a covering's
opens lies in `B`, condition (1)), and the cofinality datum in the form it is consumed —
condition (2) packaged as the section-surjectivity it produces through `ses_cech_h1`: for every
short exact sequence `S` of `O_X`-modules whose left term has vanishing higher Čech cohomology,
the section map of `S.g` is surjective over every basic open. The auxiliary `injective_acyclic`
field records the standard-cover injective Čech-acyclicity (Stacks
`lemma-injective-trivial-cech`, i.e. `injective_cech_acyclic`) for the system's coverings.
Project-local: bespoke encoding; the two sheaf-theoretic fields are discharged at the affine
(02KG) instantiation by `ses_cech_h1` + standard-cover cofinality and by `injective_cech_acyclic`
respectively. -/
structure BasisCovSystem (X : Scheme.{u}) where
  /-- The basis of opens. -/
  B : Set (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
  /-- The set of admissible coverings. -/
  Cov : Set (CovDatum X)
  /-- Condition (1): every finite intersection of a covering's opens lies in the basis. -/
  faces_mem : ∀ c ∈ Cov, ∀ (p : ℕ) (σ : Fin (p + 1) → c.1), (⨅ k, c.2 (σ k)) ∈ B
  /-- Condition (2), in the section-surjectivity shape produced by `ses_cech_h1` + cofinality. -/
  surj_of_vanishing : ∀ (S : ShortComplex X.Modules), S.ShortExact →
    (∀ c ∈ Cov, ∀ q, 0 < q →
      IsZero (cechCohomology c.2 ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj S.X₁) q)) →
    ∀ V ∈ B, Function.Surjective (ConcreteCategory.hom
      (((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj).map
        ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).map S.g)).app (Opposite.op V)))
  /-- Injective Čech-acyclicity for the system's coverings (`injective_cech_acyclic`). -/
  injective_acyclic : ∀ (I : X.Modules), Injective I → ∀ c ∈ Cov, ∀ q, 0 < q →
    IsZero (cechCohomology c.2 ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj I) q)

/-- **Vanishing higher Čech cohomology for a cover system** (Stacks 01EO condition (3)). An
`O_X`-module `F` satisfies this when `Ȟᵖ(𝒰, F) = 0` for every covering `𝒰 ∈ s.Cov` and every
`p > 0`. Stated for an arbitrary module (not necessarily quasi-coherent): the dimension-shift
induction feeds the quotient `Q = I/F` back as coefficient, and `Q` need not be quasi-coherent.
Project-local: the inductive predicate of the 01EO argument. -/
@[reducible] def HasVanishingHigherCech (s : BasisCovSystem X) (F : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ s.Cov, ∀ p, 0 < p →
    IsZero (cechCohomology c.2 ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F) p)

/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — L4 dimension-shift induction -/

-- The dimension-shift induction embeds modules into injectives, which needs
-- `EnoughInjectives X.Modules`. That instance is NOT available in Mathlib for sheaves of modules
-- (it would follow from `IsGrothendieckAbelian (SheafOfModules R)`, which is absent — see
-- `analogies/p5a.md`), so — following the project convention for the P5a derived-functor lane —
-- it is carried as an explicit hypothesis on `injSES`/L4 rather than synthesized.

/-- The injective-embedding short exact sequence `0 → F → I → I/F → 0` of an `O_X`-module `F`,
with `I = Injective.under F` the chosen injective and `I/F` its cokernel. Project-local helper for
the 01EO dimension-shift induction; carries `[EnoughInjectives X.Modules]` as a hypothesis. -/
@[reducible] private noncomputable def injSES [EnoughInjectives X.Modules] (F : X.Modules) :
    ShortComplex X.Modules :=
  ShortComplex.mk (Injective.ι F) (cokernel.π (Injective.ι F)) (cokernel.condition _)

private lemma injSES_shortExact [EnoughInjectives X.Modules] (F : X.Modules) :
    (injSES F).ShortExact :=
  ShortComplex.ShortExact.mk (ShortComplex.exact_cokernel _)

/-- **Dimension-shift induction `Hᵖ(U, F) = 0` for `p > 0` (Stacks 01EO L4).** For a cover system
`s` on a basis and any `O_X`-module `F` with vanishing higher Čech cohomology for `s`, the
absolute cohomology `Hᵖ(U, F) = Extᵖ(jShriekOU U, F)` vanishes for every basic open `U ∈ s.B` and
`p > 0`. Induction on `p`, quantified over all `F` in the inductive class: the quotient
`Q = I/F` re-enters the class (via the section Čech SES of L1 from the per-face SES, plus L2
quotient-vanishing and the cover system's injective acyclicity), the base case is L3, and the
inductive step is the covariant Ext long exact sequence. Project-local: the 01EO inductive core. -/
theorem absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_basis [EnoughInjectives X.Modules] (s : BasisCovSystem X)
    {F : X.Modules} (hF : HasVanishingHigherCech s F)
    {U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X} (hU : U ∈ s.B) {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p)
    (e : Ext (jShriekOU U) F p) : e = 0 := by
  have key : ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : X.Modules), HasVanishingHigherCech s F →
      ∀ (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X), U ∈ s.B →
        ∀ e : Ext (jShriekOU U) F (n + 1), e = 0 := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
      intro F hF U hU e
      have hS := injSES_shortExact F
      haveI : Injective (injSES F).X₂ := inferInstance
      exact absoluteCohomology_one_eq_zero_of_basis U hS
        (s.surj_of_vanishing (injSES F) hS hF U hU) e
    | succ m ih =>
      intro F hF U hU e
      have hS := injSES_shortExact F
      haveI : Injective (injSES F).X₂ := inferInstance
      -- The quotient `Q = (injSES F).X₃` again has vanishing higher Čech cohomology.
      have hQ : HasVanishingHigherCech s (injSES F).X₃ := by
        intro c hc q hq
        set P := (injSES F).map (Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X) with hP
        have hface : ∀ (pp : ℕ) (σ : Fin (pp + 1) → c.1),
            (faceShortComplex c.2 P σ).ShortExact := by
          intro pp σ
          refine faceShortComplex_shortExact_of_sheaf_ses c.2 (injSES F) hS ?_ pp σ
          intro pp' σ'
          exact s.surj_of_vanishing (injSES F) hS hF _ (s.faces_mem c hc pp' σ')
        have hSES := cechComplex_shortExact_of_basis c.2 P hface
        exact quotient_cech_vanishing_of_basis c.2 P hSES
          (s.injective_acyclic (injSES F).X₂ inferInstance c hc) (hF c hc) q hq
      -- Ext long exact sequence step: `H^{m+2}(F)` is squeezed by `H^{m+1}(Q) = 0` (IH) and
      -- `H^{m+2}(I) = 0` (injective vanishing).
      have hef : e.comp (Ext.mk₀ (injSES F).f) (add_zero (m + 1 + 1)) = 0 :=
        absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_injective (m + 1) U (injSES F).X₂ _
      obtain ⟨x₃, hx₃⟩ :=
        absoluteCohomology_covariant_exact₁ U hS e hef (rfl : (m + 1) + 1 = m + 1 + 1)
      have hx₃zero : x₃ = 0 := ih (injSES F).X₃ hQ U hU x₃
      rw [← hx₃, hx₃zero, Ext.zero_comp]
  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero hp.ne'
  exact key n F hF U hU e

/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — Čech-to-cohomology comparison on a basis (01EO top) -/

/-- **Čech-to-cohomology comparison on a basis (Stacks 01EO).** Let `s` be a cover system on a
basis for `X` and `F` an `O_X`-module with vanishing higher Čech cohomology for `s` (conditions
(1)–(3) of 01EO, packaged in `s` and `hF`). Then the absolute cohomology `Hᵖ(U, F) =
Extᵖ(jShriekOU U, F)` vanishes for every basic open `U ∈ s.B` and every `p > 0`. The thin assembly
of the dimension-shift induction `absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_basis` (L4), which itself chains
the section-Čech short exact sequence (L1), quotient vanishing (L2), and the base case (L3).
Project-local: the named 01EO target, carrying `[EnoughInjectives X.Modules]` as a hypothesis (the
instance is absent in Mathlib for sheaves of modules; see `injSES`). -/
theorem cech_eq_cohomology_of_basis [EnoughInjectives X.Modules] (s : BasisCovSystem X)
    {F : X.Modules} (hF : HasVanishingHigherCech s F) :
    ∀ U ∈ s.B, ∀ p, 0 < p → ∀ e : Ext (jShriekOU U) F p, e = 0 :=
  fun _ hU _ hp e => absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_basis s hF hU hp e

end AlgebraicGeometry

private lemma twistedSMul_smul_right_aux (F L : X.Modules) (i j : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
    (a : ↥((X.sheaf.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat).obj (op U)))
    (r : ↥(((toPresheafOfModules X).obj (tensorPow L i)).obj (op U)))
    (x : ↥(((toPresheafOfModules X).obj (moduleTensorPow F L j)).obj (op U))) :
    twistedSMul F L i j U r (a • x)
      = a • (twistedSMul F L i j U r x :
          ↥(((toPresheafOfModules X).obj (moduleTensorPow F L (i + j))).obj (op U))) := by
  unfold twistedSMul
  erw [TensorProduct.tmul_smul, _root_.map_smul, _root_.map_smul]
  rfl

    (a : Γ(X, U)) (r : Γ(tensorPow L i, U)) (x : Γ(moduleTensorPow F L j, U)) :
    twistedSMul F L i j U r (a • x)
      = a • twistedSMul F L i j U r x :=
  twistedSMul_smul_right_aux F L i j U a r x

`ModuleCat`-carrier spelling.  (Same `_root_.map_smul` qualification as in

    (r : ↥(((toPresheafOfModules X).obj (tensorPow L i)).obj (op U)))
    (x : ↥(((toPresheafOfModules X).obj (moduleTensorPow F L j)).obj (op U))) :

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.GenusFiniteness

/-!
# The last genus-finiteness gates: scoping the Čech-to-derived comparison

This file scopes the **final** gates of the adelic genus-finiteness consumable
`Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1` (`GenusFiniteness.lean`, node `N12`).
That consumable is stated under four gates:

1. `HasFiniteMapToP1 C`               — node `N9`  (curve ⟶ ℙ¹, in progress elsewhere);
2. `P1HasLaurentChartData k`          — node `N11b` (ℙ¹ chart rings, `P1ChartData.lean`);
3. `HasExt.{u}` **and** `HasExt.{u+1}` for the sheaf category
   `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`
   — the ambient `Ext`-theory the `HModule` genus carrier runs on;
4. `∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
      HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`
   — the Čech-to-derived comparison (Leray/Cartan) on 2-affine covers.

The question this file answers: **are gates 3 and 4 instantiable today?**

## Gate 3 (the `HasExt` pair): INSTANTIABLE — proved here

The genus carrier lives in the sheaf category `𝒮 := Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology
C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`, i.e. sheaves of `k`-modules for the *constant* base
field `k`.  This is the crucial point that dissolves the historical blocker: `𝒮` is a
**Grothendieck abelian category** (Mathlib `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} (Sheaf J A)` for a
small site `J` and Grothendieck-abelian `A = ModuleCat k`), so Mathlib supplies
`EnoughInjectives 𝒮` (`079H`) and both `HasExt.{u} 𝒮`, `HasExt.{u+1} 𝒮` (`HasExt.standard`)
**for free**.  See `hasExt_moduleKSheaf` / `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf` /
`enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf` / `isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf` below.

This is *not* the situation of the `SheafOfModules R = X.Modules` apparatus (`Ext` over the
structure sheaf `𝒪_X` as a sheaf of rings), which the historical Čech capstone
(`CechToCohomology.cech_eq_cohomology_of_basis`, `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing`)
runs on: there Mathlib v4.31 provides *no* Grothendieck-abelian / enough-injectives instance
for `SheafOfModules`, so every derived-functor statement in that lane carries
`[EnoughInjectives X.Modules]` / `[HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]` as an un-instantiable
hypothesis.  The genus carrier deliberately uses the constant-`k` sheaf category precisely to
avoid that trap — and the trap is genuinely avoided.

Consequence (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): gate 3 can simply be
dropped from the `N12` consumable — Mathlib synthesises it — leaving only gates 1, 2, 4.

## Gate 4 (the comparison `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso …`): NOT instantiable today

`HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` (`MayerVietorisCover.lean`) is the `Prop`-class packaging of the
comparison data `∀ n, cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)`, i.e. "for the cover
`𝒰`, unnormalised Čech cohomology equals derived (`Ext`) cohomology in every degree".

For the 2-affine cover `S.coverFamily` this comparison is *mathematically* the Leray statement
"an affine cover is acyclic ⟹ Čech computes cohomology", which for a **two**-element cover is
exactly the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence (`HModule'_sequence_exact`, in-tree) together
with **affine Serre vanishing in the constant-`k` sheaf apparatus**:
`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`, i.e. `Subsingleton (HModule' k
(toModuleKSheaf C) i U) = 0` for every affine open `U` and every `i > 0`.  Given that vanishing,
the comparison assembles degreewise: `n = 0` (sheaf axiom), `n = 1` (`cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok`
= node `N5`, in-tree, plus the MV cokernel identification), `n ≥ 2` (both sides vanish).

The **precise gap** is therefore this single named input:

> **MISSING:** `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` — Serre vanishing
> `Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_C) = 0` (`i > 0`, `U` affine) in the `Sheaf (Opens.gT …) (ModuleCat k)` apparatus,
> **plus** the degreewise assembly of the 2-cover comparison from it.

Neither piece is a one-line consequence of an existing lemma:

* Mathlib has no scheme-cohomology Serre vanishing at all, in any apparatus.
* The in-tree Serre vanishing `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing` lives in the *wrong*
  category (`X.Modules`, `Ext (jShriekOU U)`) and is itself gated on the un-instantiable
  `[EnoughInjectives (Spec R).Modules]`; bridging it to the constant-`k` apparatus would need a
  "cohomology is independent of the linear structure" comparison that is likewise absent.
* The Čech-to-derived carrier `IsAffineHModuleVanishing` is currently *produced* in-tree only
  from `HasAffineCechAcyclicCover` — which itself bundles `HasCechToHModuleIso` on the affine
  sub-covers, i.e. the very comparison we are trying to instantiate (a circular producer).

So gate 4 is a genuine multi-lemma target, **but the historical infrastructure blocker is gone**:
because `EnoughInjectives 𝒮` is now available (proved below), the honest way to close gate 4 is
to build affine Serre vanishing + the Čech comparison *directly in the constant-`k` sheaf
category* `𝒮` (where injective resolutions exist), rather than attempting to route through the
blocked `SheafOfModules` lane.  That is the recommended roadmap for the next wave.

* the gate-3 infrastructure, proved and named for citation

  `hasExt_moduleKSheaf`, `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf`);
* the gate-3-free restatement of the `N12` consumable
  (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): under gates 1, 2, 4 alone,
  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite `k`-module.  Once `P1ChartData` lands (gate 2) and the gate-4
  comparison is built, `Module.Finite k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` — hence the honesty of `genus C` — is
  unconditional on a curve with a finite map to ℙ¹.
-/

structural fact that makes the derived-functor genus apparatus well-founded (contrast the
`SheafOfModules 𝒪_X` apparatus, for which Mathlib v4.31 supplies no such instance). -/
theorem isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u}
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
  inferInstance

Grothendieck-abelianness).  This is the input the entire `Ext`/derived-functor comparison
needs, and the exact instance the `SheafOfModules 𝒪_X` lane cannot supply.  Its availability
here is what dissolves the historical Čech-capstone blocker for the *constant-`k`* apparatus. -/
theorem enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    EnoughInjectives
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
  inferInstance

/-- Gate 3, lower universe: `HasExt.{u}` for the genus-carrier sheaf category is synthesisable
(from `HasExt.standard`, itself from Grothendieck-abelianness). -/
theorem hasExt_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
  inferInstance

/-- Gate 3, upper universe: `HasExt.{u+1}` for the genus-carrier sheaf category is
synthesisable (the ambient `Ext`-theory the universe-bridged `HModule` genus carrier runs on). -/
theorem hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    HasExt.{u+1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
  inferInstance

Because both `HasExt` gates are now synthesised (gate 3 above), the `N12` consumable of

with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ and the ℙ¹ chart data, and with the Čech-to-derived comparison on

/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-012 scaffold): the `n`-th Čech cohomology
of the structure sheaf for an arbitrary indexed open cover. Defined as the
`n`-th homology of the Čech cochain complex `Scheme.cechCochain_OC`. The
result lives in `ModuleCat.{u} k` and therefore carries a `Module k`
structure for free; the iter-013+ comparison theorem will identify it
with `Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n` when the cover is
acyclic. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.cechCohomology_OC
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) (n : ℕ) :
    ModuleCat.{u} k :=
  (Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰).homology n

/-- Iter-047: parameterised Čech cochain complex generalising iter-012's
`Scheme.cechCochain_OC` to any sheaf of `k`-modules `F`, not just the structure
sheaf. Built from the same Mathlib `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`
(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Cech.lean`) applied to the
underlying presheaf of `F`. The result is a cochain complex valued in
`ModuleCat.{u} k`, indexed by `ℕ`. Iter-012's specialisation
`Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰` is recovered by setting `F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`
(see `Scheme.cechCochain_OC_eq` below).

This generalisation is the foundational scaffolding the iter-048+ Čech-vs-derived
comparison theorem will build on: the comparison map
`Scheme.cechCohomology k C F 𝒰 n →ₗ[k] Scheme.HModule' k F n (⨆ᵢ 𝒰 i)`
(queued for iter-048) is naturally parameterised over the sheaf `F`, not just
the structure sheaf, so the parameterised carrier is the right level of
generality. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.cechCochain
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) :
    CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℕ :=
  (cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F)

/-- Iter-047: parameterised Čech cohomology generalising iter-012's
`Scheme.cechCohomology_OC`. The `n`-th cohomology of the parameterised Čech
cochain complex. The result lives in `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Iter-012's
specialisation is recovered by `Scheme.cechCohomology_OC_eq` below. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.cechCohomology
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) (n : ℕ) :
    ModuleCat.{u} k :=
  (Scheme.cechCochain C F 𝒰).homology n

/-- Iter-047 bridge: iter-012's `Scheme.cechCochain_OC` is definitionally the
`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` specialisation of `Scheme.cechCochain`. The
proof is `rfl` since iter-012's body is the same `(cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj

consumers (iter-048+) to switch between the iter-012 structure-sheaf-specific
form and the iter-047 parameterised form without semantic loss. -/

61	    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C]
62	    [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} C] {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (a b : Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y n) :
63	    Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.{w'} (a + b) =

291	– (yoneda.map S.f₁₃)` lifted through the biproduct), and `g` (the sum

304	    (k : Type u) [Field k]

307	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) :
308	    ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) where
309	  X₁ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₁ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)
310	  X₂ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₂ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k) ⊞
311	    (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₃ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)
312	  X₃ := (presheafToSheaf J _).obj (yoneda.obj S.X₄ ⋙ ModuleCat.free k)

585	    (by ext; apply HModule'_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom_toBiprod_apply)
586	    (by ext; symm; apply HModule'_mk₀_f_comp_biprodAddEquiv_symm_biprodIsoProd_hom)

588	/-- Iter-026: Mayer-Vietoris LES exactness theorem (mirror Mathlib
589	`MayerVietoris.lean` L140–141). The iter-022 sequence is exact via the iter-023
590	comparison iso to `Ext.contravariantSequence`. -/
591	lemma HModule'_sequence_exact
592	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
593	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
594	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
595	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
596	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
597	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
598	    (HModule'_sequence k S F n₀ n₁ h).Exact :=
599	  ComposableArrows.exact_of_iso (HModule'_sequenceIso k S F n₀ n₁ h).symm
600	    (Abelian.Ext.contravariantSequence_exact _ _ _ _ _)
601	
602	/-- Iter-026: `δ ≫ toBiprod = 0` simp companion (mirror Mathlib L143–145). -/
603	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
604	lemma HModule'_δ_toBiprod
605	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
606	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
607	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
608	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
609	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
610	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
611	    HModule'_δ k S F n₀ n₁ h ≫ HModule'_toBiprod k S F n₁ = 0 :=
612	  (HModule'_sequence_exact k S F n₀ n₁ h).zero 2
613	
614	/-- Iter-026: `fromBiprod ≫ δ = 0` simp companion (mirror Mathlib L147–149). -/
615	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
616	lemma HModule'_fromBiprod_δ
617	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
618	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
619	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
620	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
621	    (S : J.MayerVietorisSquare) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
622	    (n₀ n₁ : ℕ) (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
623	    HModule'_fromBiprod k S F n₀ ≫ HModule'_δ k S F n₀ n₁ h = 0 :=

155	/-- Iter-031 cover-totality source-object identification. For a category `C`
156	with terminal object `T`, the sheafification of the free `k`-module on the
157	representable presheaf at `T` is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf
158	at `ModuleCat.of k k`. This is the natural-iso prerequisite for identifying
159	`HModule' k F n T` (open-evaluation cohomology at the terminal `T`, iter-014)
160	with `HModule k F n` (global cohomology, iter-009): both are `Ext` groups
161	whose source objects are made canonically isomorphic by this iso.
162	
163	Assembled from three Mathlib pieces, mirroring the structure
164	`constantSheaf J D = Functor.const Cᵒᵖ ⋙ presheafToSheaf J D`:
165	1. `yoneda.obj T ≅ (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj PUnit` — the terminal-collapse
166	   of the representable, by `IsTerminal.from`/`IsTerminal.hom_ext`.
167	2. `Functor.constComp _ PUnit (ModuleCat.free k)` — the identity
168	   `(Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj PUnit ⋙ ModuleCat.free k =
169	    (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj ((ModuleCat.free k).obj PUnit)`
170	   packaged as an iso.
171	3. `(Finsupp.LinearEquiv.finsuppUnique k k PUnit).toModuleIso` —
172	   `(ModuleCat.free k).obj PUnit ≅ ModuleCat.of k k`. -/
173	noncomputable def HModule'_top_sourceIso
174	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
175	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
176	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
177	    {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
178	    (presheafToSheaf J _).obj
179	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj T)
180	      ≅ (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) :=
181	  (presheafToSheaf J _).mapIso
182	    (Functor.isoWhiskerRight
183	        (NatIso.ofComponents
184	          (fun _ => Equiv.toIso { toFun := fun _ => PUnit.unit
185	                                  invFun := fun _ => hT.from _
186	                                  left_inv := fun _ => hT.hom_ext _ _
187	                                  right_inv := fun _ => rfl })
188	          (fun _ => by ext; rfl))
189	        (ModuleCat.free k) ≪≫
190	      Functor.constComp _ PUnit.{u+1} (ModuleCat.free k) ≪≫
191	      (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).mapIso
192	        (Finsupp.LinearEquiv.finsuppUnique k k PUnit).toModuleIso)
193	
194	/-- Iter-032 cover-totality Ext-transport at universe `u+1`. Combining the
195	iter-031 `HModule'_top_sourceIso` (a sheaf-level natural iso between source
196	objects of two `Ext` computations) with the Mathlib Ext-API operation
197	`precompOfLinear` (pre-composition of `Ext` along an `Ext 0`-element) yields
198	a `k`-linear equivalence between the universe-`u+1` Ext at the sheafified
199	representable on `T` and `HModule k F n`.
200	
201	The universe annotation `Abelian.Ext.{u+1}` on the LHS is load-bearing —
202	without it Lean would pick `Ext.{u}` (matching iter-014's `HModule'` choice),
203	and the equivalence would not typecheck against `HModule k F n : Type (u+1)`
204	(iter-009). By pinning the LHS to `Ext.{u+1}` we sidestep the iter-031
205	universe mismatch (`HModule' : Type u` vs `HModule : Type (u+1)`); both
206	sides of this equivalence live at `Type (u+1)`. The bridge from
207	`HModule' k F n T : Type u` to the LHS here is iter-033+ work — most
208	plausibly via a small refactor on iter-014 to align `HModule'`'s universe,
209	or via a `ULift.{u+1}` wrapper.
210	
211	Body uses `LinearEquiv.ofLinear` with two pre-composition maps via the
212	iter-031 iso's hom/inv. The round-trip equations close by a four-step
213	rewrite: associativity (with the middle factor degree 0), composition
214	collapse via `mk₀_comp_mk₀`, the iso identity, and `mk₀_id_comp`. -/
215	noncomputable def HModule_top_linearEquiv
216	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
217	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
218	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
219	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
220	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
221	    Abelian.Ext.{u+1}
222	        ((presheafToSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
223	          ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj T)) F n
224	      ≃ₗ[k] HModule k F n :=
225	  let α := HModule'_top_sourceIso k hT
226	  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
227	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
228	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
229	    (by
230	      ext x
231	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp
232	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp x (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = x
233	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
234	          α.inv_hom_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])
235	    (by
236	      ext y
237	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp
238	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp y (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = y
239	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
240	          α.hom_inv_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])
241	
242	/-- Iter-033 cover-totality Ext-transport at universe `u`. The universe-`u`
243	parallel of iter-032's `HModule_top_linearEquiv`. Combining the iter-031
244	`HModule'_top_sourceIso` (a sheaf-level natural iso between source objects
245	of two `Ext` computations) with the Mathlib Ext-API operation
246	`precompOfLinear` (pre-composition of `Ext` along an `Ext 0`-element)
247	yields a `k`-linear equivalence between `HModule' k F n T` (the iter-014
248	universe-`u` cohomology of an open at the terminal) and the universe-`u`
249	`Ext` at the constant sheaf on `ModuleCat.of k k`.
250	
251	Both sides live at `Type u` (matching iter-014's `HModule'` ascription).
252	This is the universe-`u` parallel of iter-032's universe-`u+1` form; the
253	final bridge between the two (`Ext.{u}((constantSheaf J _).obj
254	(ModuleCat.of k k)) F n ≃ₗ[k] HModule k F n = Ext.{u+1}(...)`) is
255	iter-034+ work, requiring Mathlib's `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv` (a bare
256	`Equiv`, file `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/Basic.lean`
257	L540) to be upgraded to a `LinearEquiv`.
258	
259	The body is shape-identical to iter-032: `LinearEquiv.ofLinear` with two
260	pre-composition maps via the iter-031 iso's hom/inv. The round-trip
261	equations close by the same four-step rewrite chain. Lean's universe
262	inference adapts automatically because the LHS `HModule' k F n T`
263	forces `Ext.{u}` everywhere. -/
264	noncomputable def HModule'_top_linearEquiv
265	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
266	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
267	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
268	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
269	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
270	    HModule' k F n T
271	      ≃ₗ[k] Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
272	              (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n :=
273	  let α := HModule'_top_sourceIso k hT
274	  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
275	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
276	    ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).precompOfLinear k F (zero_add n))
277	    (by
278	      ext x
279	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp
280	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp x (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = x
281	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
282	          α.inv_hom_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])
283	    (by
284	      ext y
285	      change (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.hom).comp
286	        ((Abelian.Ext.mk₀ α.inv).comp y (zero_add n)) (zero_add n) = y
287	      rw [← Abelian.Ext.comp_assoc_of_second_deg_zero, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀,
288	          α.hom_inv_id, Abelian.Ext.mk₀_id_comp])
289	
290	/-- Iter-034 universe-bump bridge. Composes iter-033's
291	`HModule'_top_linearEquiv` (universe-`u` cover-totality between `HModule' k F n T`
292	and `Ext.{u} ((constantSheaf J _).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n`) with the
293	universe shift `Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` (Mathlib gap-fill at the top
294	of this file) lifting the result to `Ext.{u+1} ((constantSheaf J _).obj
295	(ModuleCat.of k k)) F n = HModule k F n` (definitional unfold of the iter-009
296	abbrev). The composition gives the full bridge `HModule' k F n T ≃ₗ[k]
297	HModule k F n` for terminal `T`, closing Step 3 of the Serre-finiteness
298	scaffold. Iter-035+ specialises this to `AffineCoverMVSquare` using
299	iter-029's `toMayerVietorisSquare_toSquare_X₄ : ... = ⊤` simp lemma. -/
300	noncomputable def HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv
301	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
302	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
303	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
304	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
305	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
306	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :
307	    HModule' k F n T ≃ₗ[k] HModule k F n :=
308	  (HModule'_top_linearEquiv k F n hT).trans Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv
309	
310	/-- Iter-035 corner-bridge specialisation, abstract sheaf form. With iter-034's
311	universal bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` in scope, the natural
312	specialisation lands the bridge on the `X₄` corner of an `AffineCoverMVSquare`,
313	where iter-029's simp lemma `toMayerVietorisSquare_toSquare_X₄` identifies the
314	corner with `⊤ : Opens X.toTopCat`. Mathlib's `Preorder.isTerminalTop`
315	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preorder.lean`) supplies the
316	`IsTerminal ⊤` witness; transporting this back via the simp lemma's `.symm`
317	gives the required `IsTerminal X₄` to feed into the universal bridge. The
318	qualified `TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat` form is required to sidestep the
319	iter-029 sub-namespace shadowing trap (bare `Opens X.toTopCat` inside `def
320	AffineCoverMVSquare.foo` shadows to `Scheme.Opens` which expects a `Scheme`). -/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.StructureSheafModuleK.SheafProperty
7	
8	/-!
9	# Sheaves of `k`-modules: finite-length carriers and producer instances
10	
11	Sub-file (3/3) of the `StructureSheafModuleK` split (refactor iter-174). This file
12	hosts the downstream finite-length carriers (`IsAffineHModuleVanishing`,
13	`IsHModuleHomFinite`), their algebraic bridges (the `HModule` / `HModule'`
14	abbrevs, the H⁰ `LinearEquiv` transport companions, the constant-sheaf-Γ adjunction
15	upgrade), and the curve-side producer instances. Upstream sub-files
16	`Presheaf.lean` and `SheafProperty.lean` provide the structure-sheaf object the
17	carriers depend on.
18	
19	Downstream finite-length carriers in this file:
20	
21	* H>0 affine cohomology vanishing is carried by iter-040's
22	  `IsAffineHModuleVanishing` (the producer instance for the curve case
23	  lives at iter-051).
24	* H⁰ Hom-finiteness is carried by iter-043's **wholespace**
25	  `IsHModuleHomFinite`; the producer instance on a proper geometrically
26	  integral $k$-curve is supplied at iter-046 from Stein finiteness
27	  (`module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper`).
28	* The iter-041 per-affine-open variant `IsAffineHModuleHomFinite` was an
29	  abandoned attempt (dead scaffolding — $\Gamma(U, O_C)$ is not finite
30	  over $k$ on a proper affine open of a non-trivial curve) and has been
31	  removed from this file.
32	
33	See `blueprint/src/chapters/Cohomology_StructureSheafModuleK.tex`.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u v
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
43	
44	/-- Phase A step 5/6 bridge (iter-009 scaffold): the parallel `Sheaf.H` for
45	`ModuleCat k`-valued sheaves. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H` is
46	parameterised over `Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat` only, so closing `genus` honestly
47	requires this `ModuleCat k`-flavoured version. The result carries `Module k`
48	automatically via `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.instModule`, and
49	`Module.finrank k` is therefore well-defined on it. The declaration is a
50	`noncomputable abbrev` (rather than `def`) so that instance synthesis sees
51	through the wrapper to find `Module k` and `AddCommGroup` instances. -/
52	noncomputable abbrev HModule
53	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
54	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
55	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
56	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) : Type (u+1) :=
57	  Abelian.Ext ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k)) F n
58	
59	/-- Phase A step 6 algebraic bridge (iter-010 scaffold): the $k$-linear
60	identification of `HModule k F 0` with the Hom group from the constant
61	sheaf at `ModuleCat.of k k`. Mathlib provides
62	`CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ : Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)` in any
63	`Linear R`-enriched abelian category; specialised to the `Linear k`
64	enrichment of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` (auto-inferable from
65	`HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`), this collapses `HModule k F 0` to a
66	`k`-linear Hom group. The closure body is `Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀`;
67	probe-confirmed one-liner (iter-010 plan-agent). Used downstream to
68	identify `H⁰(C, toModuleKSheaf C)` with `Γ(C, O_C)` viewed as a
69	`k`-module on a connected proper `k`-curve. -/
70	noncomputable def HModule_zero_linearEquiv
71	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
72	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
73	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
74	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
75	    HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k]
76	      ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F) :=
77	  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀
78	
79	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-013 scaffold): the `ModuleCat k`-flavored
80	cohomology of an open `X : C` with values in a sheaf `F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`.
81	Mirrors Mathlib's `Sheaf.H' F n X = (F.cohomologyPresheaf n).obj (op X)`
82	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean` L105) for
83	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued sheaves, with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.
84	
85	The codomain is `Type u` (not `ModuleCat.{u} k`): `Abelian.Ext` returns a bare
86	`Type u` carrying `Module k` via `Abelian.Ext.instModule` through the `Linear k`
87	enrichment. The `noncomputable abbrev` form (rather than `def`) is required so
88	instance synthesis sees through the wrapper to find `Module k (HModule' k F n X)`
89	and `AddCommGroup (HModule' k F n X)` — under `def`, `Module.finrank` would fail
90	to typecheck (cf. iter-009 design rationale on `HModule`).
91	
92	This is the prerequisite for the iter-014+ `ModuleCat k`-flavored Mayer-Vietoris
93	LES (mirror of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris.lean`).
94	The iter-014+ work will state and prove the LES on a `MayerVietorisSquare`,
95	specialising to a 2-affine cover of a proper `k`-curve in iter-015+. The
96	comparison theorem `cechCohomology_OC C 𝒰 n ≅ HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) n`
97	for an acyclic cover (the technical heart of Path-2) is also queued for
98	iter-015+. -/
99	noncomputable abbrev HModule' (k : Type u) [Field k]
100	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
101	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
102	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
103	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) (X : C) : Type u :=
104	  Abelian.Ext ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
105	    ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X)) F n
106	
107	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-015): the `H⁰` algebraic bridge for `HModule'`,
108	mirroring iter-010's `HModule_zero_linearEquiv` for the iter-014 `HModule'`. The
109	$k$-linear identification of `HModule' k F 0 X` with the Hom group from the
110	sheafified representable `(presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X)`.
111	Mathlib provides `CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ : Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)`
112	in any `Linear R`-enriched abelian category; specialised to `R = k` and to the
113	`Linear k`-enriched abelian category `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` (the `Linear k`
114	enrichment is auto-inferable from `HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` via Mathlib's
115	`Sheaf.linear`), this collapses `HModule' k F 0 X` to a `k`-linear Hom group. The
116	closure body is `Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀`; probe-confirmed one-liner (iter-015
117	plan-agent). Used downstream as the algebraic prerequisite for Stein-factorization-
118	derived `H⁰(C, O_C) ≃ k` on a connected proper `k`-curve (multi-iteration; queued
119	iter-017+ alongside the Mayer-Vietoris LES of iter-016+). -/
120	noncomputable def HModule'_zero_linearEquiv
121	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
122	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
123	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
124	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
125	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C) :
126	    HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
127	      ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
128	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F) :=
129	  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀
130	
131	/-- Iter-038 `Module.Finite` H⁰ transport companion for `HModule k F 0`. The iter-010
132	H⁰ bridge `HModule_zero_linearEquiv : HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k] ((constantSheaf J _).obj
133	(ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)` identifies the degree-zero cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom
134	group; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness across.
135	The `.symm` is required: iter-010's bridge has `HModule k F 0` on the LHS and the
136	Hom group on the RHS, but we want the Hom hypothesis on the LHS and the
137	`HModule` conclusion on the RHS, so we apply `.symm` first. Mirrors iter-037's
138	`module_finite_HModule_of_HModule'_X₄` pattern at degree $0$, with no Mayer-Vietoris
139	machinery required. Used downstream as a building block for `Module.Finite k
140	(HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` once the Hom-from-constant-sheaf finiteness
141	input is supplied for proper geometrically integral $k$-curves. -/
142	theorem module_finite_HModule_zero
143	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
144	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
145	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
146	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
147	    [Module.Finite k ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)] :
148	    Module.Finite k (HModule k F 0) :=
149	  Module.Finite.equiv (HModule_zero_linearEquiv k F).symm
150	
151	/-- Iter-038 `Module.Finite` H⁰ transport companion for `HModule' k F 0 X`. Parallel
152	of `Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero` for the iter-014 sheaf-parameterised carrier
153	`HModule'`. The iter-015 H⁰ bridge `HModule'_zero_linearEquiv : HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
154	((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X) ⟶ F)` identifies the
155	degree-zero open-evaluation cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom group from the sheafified
156	representable; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness
157	across. The `.symm` is required for the same orientation reason as in
158	`Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero`. -/
159	theorem module_finite_HModule'_zero
160	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
161	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
162	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
163	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
164	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C)
165	    [Module.Finite k ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
166	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F)] :
167	    Module.Finite k (HModule' k F 0 X) :=
168	  Module.Finite.equiv (HModule'_zero_linearEquiv k F X).symm
169	
170	/-- Iter-039 curve specialisation of iter-038's `module_finite_HModule_zero` to
171	the structure sheaf `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` of a `Spec k`-scheme `C`. The
172	Grothendieck topology `Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat` is auto-inferred
173	via the iter-005 instances `instHasSheafify_Opens_ModuleCatK` and
174	`instHasExt_Sheaf_Opens_ModuleCatK`. The sheaf argument is inferred from the
175	result type. Mirrors iter-030 / iter-035 / iter-036 / iter-037's `_curve`
176	patterns. Used downstream as a building block for `Module.Finite k (HModule k
177	(toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` once the Hom-from-constant-sheaf finiteness input is
178	supplied for proper geometrically integral $k$-curves (typically the morally
179	trivial `H^0(C, O_C) ≃ k` from Stein factorization on a connected proper
180	curve). -/
181	theorem module_finite_HModule_zero_curve
182	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
183	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
184	    [Module.Finite k
185	      ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
186	        (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)] :
187	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 0) :=
188	  Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero k _
189	
190	/-- Iter-039 curve specialisation of iter-038's `module_finite_HModule'_zero` to
191	the structure sheaf `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` of a `Spec k`-scheme `C`,
192	evaluated at an arbitrary open `U` of the underlying topological space. Parallel
193	of `module_finite_HModule_zero_curve` for the iter-014 sheaf-parameterised
194	carrier `HModule'`.  Same auto-inferred topology / instance setup. The open `U`
195	is an explicit parameter (unlike the implicit topology); the sheaf argument is
196	inferred. Used downstream in the cover-evaluation chain for proper geometrically
197	integral $k$-curves: for each affine corner $X_i$ of an `AffineCoverMVSquare`,
198	the iter-039 transport propagates `Module.Finite k`-ness from the Hom group
199	`((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ free_k).obj X_i) ⟶ toModuleKSheaf C)` —
200	morally `Module.Finite k (Γ(X_i, O_C))` for affine $X_i$ — to the H⁰ cohomology
201	piece `HModule' k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0 X_i`. -/

309	/-- Iter-044 geometric Stein input for the iter-043 wholespace H⁰
310	Hom-finiteness carrier. For `C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))` an
311	integral $k$-scheme with proper structure morphism, the global sections
312	$\Gamma(C, O_C)$ form a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space.
313	
314	This is Stein's classical statement, packaged via Mathlib's
315	`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`
316	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`):
317	for $X$ integral and $f \colon X \to \Spec K$ universally closed and
318	locally of finite type, the structure-morphism ring map `f.appTop`
319	is module-finite. `IsProper f` packages both `UniversallyClosed f` and
320	`LocallyOfFiniteType f`.
321	
322	The bridge from `RingHom.Finite (C.hom.appTop.hom)` to
323	`Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))` (where the algebra
324	structure on `Γ(C, ⊤)` is iter-006's `kToSection`-derived) uses
325	`RingHom.finite_algebraMap` plus `Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv` to
326	transport the base ring from intermediate `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)` to `k` along
327	the ring iso `Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)`. The compatibility
328	of algebra maps reduces to showing
329	`kToSection C (op ⊤).hom = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).inv.hom`,
330	which collapses via `Subsingleton.elim` on the `⊤ ⟶ ⊤` hom-set +
331	`Functor.map_id`.
332	
333	Iter-045+ consumes this input to assemble the producer instance
334	`IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` via lifting Mathlib's
335	`constantSheafΓAdj.homEquiv` to a `LinearEquiv` + identification of
336	`Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C)` with the underlying global sections
337	+ transport via `Module.Finite.equiv`. -/
338	theorem module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper
339	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
340	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
341	    Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
342	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
343	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
344	  letI alg2 : Algebra ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
345	               (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
346	    := RingHom.toAlgebra C.hom.appTop.hom
347	  have hM_inter :
348	      Module.Finite ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
349	        (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
350	    rw [← RingHom.finite_algebraMap]; exact hf
351	  refine Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv
352	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
353	    (RingEquiv.refl _) ?_
354	  ext x
355	  simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.refl_apply,
356	    Function.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
357	  have h_kts : (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)).hom =
358	                (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
359	    ext y
360	    simp only [Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
361	      RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
362	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ :
363	                TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)))) _
364	  calc (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)))
365	        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x)
366	       = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom)
367	          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x) :=
368	              congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe h_kts) _
369	    _  = C.hom.appTop.hom x := by
370	        simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
371	        congr 1
372	        change ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).hom ≫
373	              (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv).hom x = x
374	        rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]; rfl

376	/-- Iter-045: LinearEquiv between the global-sections module
377	`(Sheaf.Γ J _).obj F` (an object of `ModuleCat k`) and the underlying carrier
378	of `F.obj.obj (op ⊤)` for any sheaf `F` on a topological space `X`.
379	
380	The underlying iso comes from `Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections` (Mathlib
381	`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/GlobalSections.lean`): on a site with terminal
382	`T`, the global-sections functor is naturally iso to evaluation at `T`. For
383	the topology of opens `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, the terminal in
384	`TopologicalSpace.Opens X` is the top open `⊤` (this is `Preorder.isTerminalTop`
385	for any preorder with a top element). The categorical iso in `ModuleCat k` is
386	converted to a `LinearEquiv` via `Iso.toLinearEquiv` (Mathlib's standard
387	upgrading of `ModuleCat`-isos to LinearEquivs).
388	
389	Iter-046+ uses this `LinearEquiv` together with the linearised constant-sheaf
390	/ global-sections adjunction (multi-iteration; project-local lift of
391	Mathlib's `Adjunction.homAddEquiv` to `≃ₗ[k]`) to construct the producer
392	instance `IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`. -/
393	noncomputable def SheafGammaObj_linearEquiv_top
394	    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : TopCat.{u}}
395	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
396	    (Sheaf.Γ (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj F
397	      ≃ₗ[k] F.obj.obj (Opposite.op (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)) :=
398	  ((Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
399	      (ModuleCat.{u} k) (T := ⊤) (Preorder.isTerminalTop _)).app F).toLinearEquiv

401	/-- Iter-045 immediate consumer: combining iter-044's geometric Stein input
402	`module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper` with `SheafGammaObj_linearEquiv_top`
403	yields `Module.Finite k ((Sheaf.Γ).obj (toModuleKSheaf C))` for a proper
404	integral `Spec k`-scheme `C`.

406	The `haveI` is necessary because `Module.Finite.equiv` does not
407	auto-synthesise the `[Module.Finite k]` hypothesis on the source: the iter-044

416	requires the linearised constant-sheaf-Γ adjunction, which is multi-iteration
417	project-local infrastructure. -/
418	theorem module_finite_gammaObj_of_isProper
419	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
420	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
421	    Module.Finite k
422	      ((Sheaf.Γ (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
423	        (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)) := by
424	  haveI : Module.Finite k
425	      ((Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C).obj.obj
426	        (Opposite.op (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)) : ModuleCat k) :=
427	    module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper k C

431	/-- Iter-046: applied LinearEquiv from the constant-sheaf-Γ adjunction. For any
432	sheaf `F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat k)` and `X : ModuleCat k`, gives a `k`-LinearEquiv
433	between the Hom group `((constantSheaf).obj X ⟶ F)` (sheaf morphisms from the
434	constant sheaf at `X`) and `(X ⟶ (Sheaf.Γ).obj F)` (module morphisms into the
435	global sections of `F`).

437	Built from `(constantSheafΓAdj).homLinearEquiv` (iter-046 Mathlib gap-fill).
438	The five `haveI` lines establish the typeclass scaffolding required to invoke
439	the gap-fill: `presheafToSheaf` Linear (via `sheafificationAdjunction`),
440	`constantSheaf` Additive + Linear (via composition), and `Sheaf.Γ` Additive +
441	Linear (via the `right_adjoint_*` propagators along `constantSheafΓAdj`).
442	
443	Used in iter-046's producer instance `instIsHModuleHomFinite_toModuleKSheaf`
444	to bridge from `Sheaf.Γ.obj`-finiteness (iter-045) to Hom-from-constantSheaf-
445	finiteness (the `IsHModuleHomFinite` carrier). -/
446	noncomputable def constantSheafGammaHom_linearEquiv
447	    (k : Type u) [Field k] {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C]
448	    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
449	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasGlobalSectionsFunctor J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
450	    (X : ModuleCat.{u} k) (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
451	    ((constantSheaf J _).obj X ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[k] (X ⟶ (Sheaf.Γ J _).obj F) :=
452	  haveI : (presheafToSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).Linear k :=
453	    (sheafificationAdjunction J _).left_adjoint_linear k
454	  haveI : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).Additive := by
455	    unfold constantSheaf; infer_instance
456	  haveI : (Sheaf.Γ J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).Additive :=
457	    (constantSheafΓAdj J _).right_adjoint_additive
458	  haveI : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).Linear k := by
459	    unfold constantSheaf; infer_instance
460	  haveI : (Sheaf.Γ J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).Linear k :=
461	    (constantSheafΓAdj J _).right_adjoint_linear k
462	  (constantSheafΓAdj J _).homLinearEquiv k X F

464	/-- Iter-046: Hom-from-`k` upgrade. The Hom group `(ModuleCat.of k k ⟶ M)` for
465	`M : ModuleCat k` is canonically `k`-LinearEquivalent to `M` via `f ↦ f 1`.

467	LinearEquiv-version of the underlying-LinearMap correspondence) with
468	`LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf` (the standard `(R →ₗ[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M` evaluation). -/

471	  (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (M := ModuleCat.of k k) (N := M) (S := k)).trans
472	    (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf k k M)

474	/-- Iter-046: **the producer instance** for `IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`
475	on a proper integral `Spec k`-scheme `C`. Closes the four-step chain:
476	
477	  (1) `constantSheafGammaHom_linearEquiv` (iter-046 step 1) bridges the Hom group
478	      `((constantSheaf).obj k ⟶ toModuleKSheaf C)` to `(k ⟶ Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C))`.
479	  (2) `homFromOne_linearEquiv` (iter-046 step 3) identifies `(k ⟶ M)` with `M`
480	      as `k`-modules.
481	  (3) Combined LinearEquiv from (1)+(2): `((constantSheaf).obj k ⟶ toModuleKSheaf C)
482	      ≃ₗ[k] Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C)`.
483	  (4) `module_finite_gammaObj_of_isProper` (iter-045 step 2) provides
484	      `Module.Finite k (Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C))` from `[IsIntegral C.left]
485	      [IsProper C.hom]` (iter-044 geometric Stein input).
486	  (5) Transport via `Module.Finite.equiv (.symm)` of the combined LinearEquiv.
487	
488	Once landed, iter-043's curve consumer `module_finite_HModule_zero_of_isHModuleHomFinite_curve`
489	fires automatically on `Module.Finite k (HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` queries,
490	closing the H⁰ side of the genus-finrank Module.Finite ladder.
491	
492	Marked `instance` (not `theorem`) — this is a *producer* of a typeclass instance,
493	to be picked up by typeclass synthesis when the consumer asks for
494	`IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`. Hypotheses `[IsIntegral C.left]`,
495	`[IsProper C.hom]` are class arguments propagated via instance synthesis from
496	the use site (where `C` is concretely a proper integral `Spec k`-scheme, e.g.\ a
497	smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve). -/
498	noncomputable instance instIsHModuleHomFinite_toModuleKSheaf
499	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
500	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
501	    IsHModuleHomFinite k C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) where
502	  module_finite_hom := by
503	    haveI := Scheme.module_finite_gammaObj_of_isProper k C
504	    let LE1 := constantSheafGammaHom_linearEquiv k
505	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.of k k)
506	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)
507	    let LE2 := homFromOne_linearEquiv k
508	      ((Sheaf.Γ (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj
509	        (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C))
510	    exact Module.Finite.equiv (LE1.trans LE2).symm

547	/-- Iter-047: parameterised Čech cochain complex generalising iter-012's
548	`Scheme.cechCochain_OC` to any sheaf of `k`-modules `F`, not just the structure
549	sheaf. Built from the same Mathlib `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`
550	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Cech.lean`) applied to the
551	underlying presheaf of `F`. The result is a cochain complex valued in
552	`ModuleCat.{u} k`, indexed by `ℕ`. Iter-012's specialisation
553	`Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰` is recovered by setting `F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`
554	(see `Scheme.cechCochain_OC_eq` below).

556	This generalisation is the foundational scaffolding the iter-048+ Čech-vs-derived
557	comparison theorem will build on: the comparison map
558	`Scheme.cechCohomology k C F 𝒰 n →ₗ[k] Scheme.HModule' k F n (⨆ᵢ 𝒰 i)`
559	(queued for iter-048) is naturally parameterised over the sheaf `F`, not just
560	the structure sheaf, so the parameterised carrier is the right level of
561	generality. -/
562	noncomputable def Scheme.cechCochain
563	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
564	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))

567	  (cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F)
568

570	`Scheme.cechCohomology_OC`. The `n`-th cohomology of the parameterised Čech
571	cochain complex. The result lives in `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Iter-012's
572	specialisation is recovered by `Scheme.cechCohomology_OC_eq` below. -/

575	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))

577	    ModuleCat.{u} k :=

581	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` specialisation of `Scheme.cechCochain`. The

583	((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C))` term. Used by downstream
584	consumers (iter-048+) to switch between the iter-012 structure-sheaf-specific
585	form and the iter-047 parameterised form without semantic loss. -/

588	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) :
589	    Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰 = Scheme.cechCochain C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 :=

591

593	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` specialisation of `Scheme.cechCohomology`. -/

602	*Čech-acyclic for the sheaf `F` of `k`-modules* on `C` if positive-degree Čech

607	vanishing condition that downstream consumers receive as an instance argument.

609	This is the foundational Čech-side input that the iter-051 producer instance for

614	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))

635	theorem Scheme.subsingleton_HModule'_supr_of_isCechAcyclicCover
636	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
637	    {F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)}
638	    {ι : Type u} {𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat}

646	    (F := F) (𝒰 := 𝒰) n hn

657	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
658	    {ι : Type u} {𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat}
659	    [Scheme.IsCechAcyclicCover (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰]
660	    (compIso : ∀ (n : ℕ),

664	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n (⨆ i, 𝒰 i)) :=

4	Authors: Christian Merten

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietorisCover
7	
8	/-!
9	# The 2-cover Čech cokernel `Ȟ¹(D)` for adelic Riemann–Roch (nodes N5–N7)
10	
11	This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane** (see the lane design document).
12	It realises the degree-`1` cohomology of a curve as the concrete cokernel of a
13	two-chart cover — the algebraic incarnation of Weil's repartition quotient
14	`A_K / (A_K(D) + K)`.
15	
16	## The bridge from genus `H¹` to the Čech `H¹` (node N6)
17	
18	The project's genus carrier is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1`.
19	For a cover `𝒰` of `C` with `⨆ 𝒰 = ⊤` that is a **good** (Leray) cover — i.e. one
20	for which the Čech-to-derived comparison `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` holds — there is a
21	`k`-linear identification
22	```
23	HModule k F 1  ≃ₗ[k]  cechCohomology C F 𝒰 1,
24	```
25	obtained by chaining the comparison iso `cechToHModuleIso` (iter-050) with the
26	universe bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` (iter-034) at the terminal open
27	`⊤ = ⨆ 𝒰`.  This is `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`.
28	
29	The hypothesis `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` is the existing project **gate** (a
30	single-field `Prop` class with no unconditional instance for a 2-affine cover of a
31	positive-genus curve): the equivalence is delivered *conditional* on that class,
32	exactly as the design intends.  Note that `IsCechAcyclicCover F 𝒰` for the whole
33	curve is **not** available (nor true) here: for a genus-`g` curve the degree-`1`
34	Čech cohomology of a 2-affine cover is `k^g ≠ 0`, so it is deliberately *not*
35	assumed — the comparison `HasCechToHModuleIso` (which does *not* force the
36	cohomology to vanish) is the correct and honest hypothesis.
37	
38	## The concrete section-level cokernel (node N5 target, definition)
39	
40	For a bundled 2-affine cover `S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare` and a sheaf `F` of
41	`k`-modules, the **difference-of-restrictions** map
42	```
43	δ : Γ(U₁, F) × Γ(U₂, F) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, F),   (a, b) ↦ a|_{U₁∩U₂} − b|_{U₁∩U₂}
44	```
45	is `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiff`.  Its cokernel `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok`
46	is the concrete `Ȟ¹`, and its kernel `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionGlue` is the
47	`H⁰ = L(D)` sheaf-gluing space (global sections `= { f : agree on the overlap }`).
48	
49	Because `F` is an arbitrary sheaf of `k`-modules, `H1Cok S F` is *already* the
50	divisor-twisted `Ȟ¹(D)`: specialising `F := 𝒪_C(D)` once N3's `sectionOfDivisor`
51	lands recovers the `H¹(D)` of the χ-ledger.
52	
53	## The concrete 2-cover family and the N6 bridge on it (this wave)
54	
55	`AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily : ULift (Fin 2) → Opens X` packages `U₁, U₂` as the
56	`Type u`-indexed family that `Scheme.cechCohomology` / the N6 bridge consume, with
57	`iSup_coverFamily : ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤` the family-form of the cover totality.
58	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_coverFamily` then lands the N6 bridge on this
59	concrete family: `HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily n` (gated on
60	`HasCechToHModuleIso F S.coverFamily`).  Chaining node N5 (below) into this at `n = 1`
61	gives the lane's consumable corollary `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`.
62	
63	## The N5 identification `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F` (PROVED)
64	
65	The in-tree `cechCohomology` is the homology of Mathlib's **unnormalized**
66	`cechComplexFunctor` (`FormalCoproduct.cochainComplexFunctor` of the Čech nerve): in
67	degree `n` the product runs over **all** `Fin (n+1) → ι` (not just increasing
68	multi-indices), and the differential `dⁿ = ∑_{i} (-1)^i δⁱ` is the alternating sum of
69	the cosimplicial cofaces `δⁱ = evalOp(P)(mapPower δ_i)` (a `Pi.lift` of projections to
70	`x ∘ δ_i` followed by the restriction `P(⨅ U∘(x∘δ_i)) → P(⨅ U∘x)`).  For the 2-element
71	cover (`ι = ULift (Fin 2)`) this is
72	```
73	  M⁰ = Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁)                         (indices Fin 1 → ι)
74	  M¹ = Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₀₁) × Γ(U₀₁) × Γ(U₁)       (indices (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1))
75	  M² = ∏ over the 8 indices Fin 3 → ι         (incl. the degenerate diagonals)
76	```
77	where `Γ(U₀₁) = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`, and the two diagonal factors of `M¹` are the degenerate
78	cofaces `U_i ⊓ U_i = U_i`.  Writing a degree-1 cochain as `(p, q, r, s)`:
79	
80	* `d⁰(a, b) = (0, b|₀₁ − a|₀₁, a|₀₁ − b|₀₁, 0)`, so
81	  `im d⁰ = { (0, w, −w, 0) : w ∈ range (S.sectionDiff F) }` (note `w = b|₀₁ − a|₀₁` and
82	  `sectionDiff (a,b) = a|₀₁ − b|₀₁ = −w`, whence the images coincide as subgroups);
83	* `(d¹ n)_{(x₀,x₁,x₂)} = n_{(x₁,x₂)}| − n_{(x₀,x₂)}| + n_{(x₀,x₁)}|`.  The eight
84	  components force, after restriction (each triple intersection collapses to `U₀`, `U₁`
85	  or `U₀ ⊓ U₁`): the diagonals `p = s = 0` (from `x = (0,0,0)` and `(1,1,1)`) and
86	  `r = −q` (from `x = (0,1,0)` / `(1,0,1)`), the remaining four being automatic.  Hence
87	  `ker d¹ = { (0, q, −q, 0) : q ∈ Γ(U₀₁) } ≅ Γ(U₀₁)` via `q`.
88	
89	Therefore `H¹ = ker d¹ / im d⁰ ≅ Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) / range (S.sectionDiff F) = H1Cok S F`, the
90	iso being `[(0, q, −q, 0)] ↦ [q]`.  The identification is **unconditional** (no
91	acyclicity hypothesis — it is a pure homological-algebra fact about this specific
92	2-cover complex), and it is carried out in full in this file:
93	
94	* `sectionRestrict_trans`/`sectionRestrict_self`/`restrict_map_comp`/
95	  `restrict_map_self`/`isIso_restrict_map` — the poset restriction calculus every
96	  cancellation step reduces to;
97	* `cechD01`/`cechD12` with `cechD01_π`/`cechD12_π` — the low-degree differentials in
98	  product-typed, componentwise form;
99	* `overlapCocycle` with `overlapCocycle_comp_d` — the cocycle `q ↦ (0, q, −q, 0)`
100	  and the 8-index cancellation;
101	* `ker_cechD12_π_diag_zero₀`/`₁`, `ker_cechD12_π_off_diag`, `overlapKerEquiv` — the
102	  kernel description `ker d¹ = {(0, q, −q, 0)} ≃ₗ Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`;
103	* `pairLift`/`pairProj`/`pairLift_comp_cechD01`/`map_range_pairDiff` — the image
104	  identification `im d⁰ = κ(im sectionDiff)`;
105	* `cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok` — node N5 proper, assembled through
106	  `isoSc' 0 1 2` and `ShortComplex.moduleCatHomologyIso`;
107	* `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok` — the N5+N6 consumable
108	  `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F` under the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate.
109	-/
110	
111	set_option autoImplicit false
112	
113	universe u v
114	
115	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
116	
117	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
118	
119	/-! ## Node N6 — the `k`-linear bridge `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F 𝒰 1` -/
120	
121	/-- **Node N6 (bridge), abstract sheaf form.** For a sheaf `F` of `k`-modules on a
122	`Spec k`-scheme `C` and a cover `𝒰` with `⨆ 𝒰 = ⊤` satisfying the Čech-to-derived
123	comparison gate `HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰`, the genus-degree cohomology
124	`HModule k F n` is `k`-linearly identified with the Čech cohomology
125	`cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n` of the cover.
126	
127	The equivalence chains the iter-050 comparison
128	`cechToHModuleIso n : cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)` with the
129	iter-034 universe bridge `HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv` at the terminal open
130	`⊤ = ⨆ 𝒰` (using `Preorder.isTerminalTop` transported along `h`, exactly the
131	iter-035 `HModule'_X₄_linearEquiv` pattern), then symmetrises.
132	
133	This is stated *conditional* on the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate — no new `sorry` or
134	gate is introduced.  Downstream (`N5`, the finiteness keystone `N11`/`N12`) the
135	useful degree is `n = 1`: it reduces `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` to the concrete Čech `H¹`. -/
136	noncomputable def hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology
137	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
138	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
139	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
140	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
141	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
142	    [HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰]
143	    (h : ⨆ i, 𝒰 i = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
144	    HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n :=
145	  ((cechToHModuleIso n).trans
146	    (HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv k F n
147	      (h.symm ▸ Preorder.isTerminalTop (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)))).symm
148	
149	/-- **Node N6 (bridge), curve specialisation.** Direct application of
150	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` to the structure sheaf
151	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`.  Mirrors the iter-039/…/iter-050 `_curve` pattern
152	(dot-notation resolution against the structure sheaf), giving
153	`HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C (toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n`. -/
154	noncomputable def hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_curve
155	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
156	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
157	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
158	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
159	    [HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰]
160	    (h : ⨆ i, 𝒰 i = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
161	    HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n
162	      ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n :=
163	  hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 h n
164	
165	/-! ## Node N5 — the concrete 2-element cover family of an `AffineCoverMVSquare` -/
166	
167	/-- **The 2-element open cover family `𝒰 : ULift (Fin 2) → Opens X` of an
168	`AffineCoverMVSquare`.** Indexed by `ULift.{u} (Fin 2)` (the `Type u` two-element
169	index that `Scheme.cechCohomology`/`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` consume),
170	it sends the first index to `U₁` and the second to `U₂`.  This is the family whose
171	Čech cohomology `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1` is identified with the concrete
172	cokernel `H1Cok S F` (node N5 proper) and fed into the N6 bridge. -/
173	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
174	    ULift.{u} (Fin 2) → TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat :=
175	  fun i => if i.down = 0 then S.U₁ else S.U₂
176	
177	@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
178	    S.coverFamily ⟨0⟩ = S.U₁ := rfl
179	
180	@[simp] lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.coverFamily_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
181	    S.coverFamily ⟨1⟩ = S.U₂ := rfl
182	
183	/-- **Cover totality of `coverFamily`.** The 2-element family covers `X`:
184	`⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤`.  This is the `ι → Opens`-family incarnation of the
185	`AffineCoverMVSquare.cover` field `U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤`, and is the hypothesis
186	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` requires to land the N6 bridge on the whole
187	curve. -/
188	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.iSup_coverFamily {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
189	    ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i = ⊤ := by
190	  refine le_antisymm le_top ?_
191	  have h : S.U₁ ⊔ S.U₂ ≤ ⨆ i, S.coverFamily i :=
192	    sup_le (le_iSup_of_le ⟨0⟩ (le_of_eq S.coverFamily_zero.symm))
193	      (le_iSup_of_le ⟨1⟩ (le_of_eq S.coverFamily_one.symm))
194	  exact S.cover ▸ h
195	
196	/-- **Node N6 bridge on the concrete 2-cover family.** The specialisation of
197	`hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology` to `S.coverFamily`, discharging the totality
198	hypothesis with `iSup_coverFamily`: for a sheaf `F` of `k`-modules on the curve `C`
199	satisfying the Čech-to-derived comparison gate on the 2-affine cover, the
200	genus-degree cohomology `HModule k F n` is `k`-linearly identified with the Čech
201	cohomology `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily n` of the concrete 2-element cover.
202	Chaining node N5's `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F` into this (at
203	`n = 1`) delivers the lane's consumable `HModule k F 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`. -/
204	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology_coverFamily
205	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
206	    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
207	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
208	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
209	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
210	    [HasCechToHModuleIso F S.coverFamily]
211	    (n : ℕ) :
212	    HModule k F n ≃ₗ[k] cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily n :=
213	  hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology F S.coverFamily S.iSup_coverFamily n
214	
215	/-! ## Node N5 target — the concrete section-level difference map and cokernel -/
216	
217	section ConcreteCokernel
218	
219	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	  (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))

276	/-! ## Node N5 — concrete component formulas for the unnormalized Čech differential
277	
278	The in-tree `cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n = (cechCochain C F 𝒰).homology n` is the homology of
279	Mathlib's unnormalized `cechComplexFunctor`, routed through
280	`FormalCoproduct.cochainComplexFunctor = cosimplicialObjectFunctor ⋙ alternatingCofaceMapComplex`.
281	There is no cosimplicial dual of `alternatingFaceMapComplex_obj_d` in Mathlib, so the concrete
282	`Pi.π`-component formulas for the differential are derived here directly by unfolding the
283	alternating coface sum.  These are the reusable foundation the degree-`1` identification
284	(`cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`) is built on:
285	
286	* `cechCosimplicial_δ_π` — the single-coface component
287	  `Yδᵢ ≫ πⱼ = π_{j∘δᵢ} ≫ (reindex restriction)`;
288	* `prodOpens_eq_iInf` — the abstract Čech product object `∏ᶜ (𝒰∘j)` is the concrete infimum
289	  `⨅ₐ 𝒰(j a)` of opens (equality in the poset `Opens X`), the bridge to `Γ(⨅ₐ Uₐ)`;
290	* `alternatingCofaceMapComplex_objD` — the differential is the alternating coface sum (the
291	  missing Mathlib dual);
292	* `cechCochain_d01_π` / `cechCochain_d12_π` — the degree-`0`/degree-`1` differentials,
293	  componentwise.
294	-/

296	section CechDifferential
297	
298	open AlgebraicTopology CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits
299	
300	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
301	  {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
302	  (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
303	
304	/-- **The alternating coface differential (Mathlib dual, project-local).** The degree-`n`
305	differential of `alternatingCofaceMapComplex` is the alternating sum of coface maps
306	`objD Y n = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ • Yδᵢ`.  Mathlib has `alternatingFaceMapComplex_obj_d` but no cosimplicial
307	dual; this recreates it (the same one-line `CochainComplex.of` unfolding). -/
308	theorem alternatingCofaceMapComplex_objD {D : Type*} [Category D] [Preadditive D]
309	    (Y : CosimplicialObject D) (n : ℕ) :
310	    ((alternatingCofaceMapComplex D).obj Y).d n (n + 1)
311	      = AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD Y n := by
312	  simp only [alternatingCofaceMapComplex, AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj, CochainComplex.of_d]
313	
314	/-- The cosimplicial object underlying the Čech complex `cechCochain C F 𝒰`: it sends `⦋n⦌` to
315	`∏_{i : Fin (n+1) → ι} Γ(⨅ₐ 𝒰(i a), F)`.  `cechCochain C F 𝒰` is by definition
316	`alternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj (cechCosimplicial 𝒰 F)`. -/
317	noncomputable def cechCosimplicial : CosimplicialObject (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
318	  (FormalCoproduct.cosimplicialObjectFunctor (FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).cech).obj
319	    ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F)
320	
321	lemma cechCochain_eq :
322	    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechCochain C F 𝒰
323	      = (alternatingCofaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (cechCosimplicial 𝒰 F) :=
324	  rfl

326	/-- **Single-coface component of the Čech cosimplicial object.** The `i₀`-th coface map
327	`Yδ_{i₀} : Č^n ⟶ Č^{n+1}`, projected to the factor indexed by `j : Fin (n+2) → ι`, is the factor
328	`j ∘ δ_{i₀}` of the source followed by the reindexing restriction
329	`Γ(⨅ₐ 𝒰(j(δ_{i₀} a))) ⟶ Γ(⨅ₐ 𝒰(j a))`.  Derived by unfolding
330	`cosimplicialObjectFunctor` (`evalOp` of the Čech nerve) and `Pi.lift ≫ Pi.π`. -/
331	theorem cechCosimplicial_δ_π (n : ℕ) (i₀ : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 2) → ι) :
332	    (cechCosimplicial 𝒰 F).δ i₀ ≫ Pi.π _ j
333	      = Pi.π _ (j ∘ (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i₀)) ≫
334	          ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).map
335	            (Pi.lift (fun a => Pi.π ((FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).obj ∘ j)
336	              ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i₀) a))).op := by
337	  simp only [cechCosimplicial, CosimplicialObject.δ,
338	    FormalCoproduct.cosimplicialObjectFunctor_obj_map]
339	  erw [Limits.Pi.lift_π]
340	  rfl
341	
342	/-- **The abstract Čech product is the concrete infimum of opens.** In the poset `Opens X` the
343	categorical product `∏ᶜ (𝒰∘j)` of the family `a ↦ 𝒰 (j a)` equals its infimum `⨅ₐ 𝒰 (j a)`.
344	This is the bridge identifying the Čech section groups `Γ(∏ᶜ 𝒰∘j, F)` with the concrete
345	`Γ(⨅ₐ 𝒰(j a), F)` (and, for the 2-cover, with `Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂)`). -/
346	theorem prodOpens_eq_iInf {m : ℕ} (j : Fin m → ι) :
347	    (∏ᶜ ((FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).obj ∘ j) : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
348	      = ⨅ a, 𝒰 (j a) :=
349	  le_antisymm (le_iInf fun a => (Limits.Pi.π ((FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).obj ∘ j) a).le)
350	    (Limits.Pi.lift (fun a => homOfLE (iInf_le (fun a => 𝒰 (j a)) a))).le
351	
352	/-- The Čech face inclusion: the full intersection `∏ᶜ (𝒰∘j) = ⨅_{Fin (n+2)} 𝒰(j b)` is contained
353	in the face intersection `∏ᶜ (𝒰∘(j∘δ_{i₀})) = ⨅_{Fin (n+1)} 𝒰(j(δ_{i₀} a))` (dropping one index),
354	the `≤` of opens underlying the restriction that the coface map applies. -/
355	theorem prodOpens_δ_le {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 2) → ι) :
356	    (∏ᶜ ((FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).obj ∘ j) : TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)
357	      ≤ ∏ᶜ ((FormalCoproduct.mk _ 𝒰).obj ∘ (j ∘ Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i₀)) := by
358	  rw [prodOpens_eq_iInf, prodOpens_eq_iInf]
359	  exact le_iInf fun a => iInf_le (fun b => 𝒰 (j b)) (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i₀ a)

80	Goal: construct a cochain-complex isomorphism

82	where:
83	  • `K(𝒰)_p = ∐_{σ : Fin(p+1) → 𝒰.I₀} freeYoneda.obj (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ)`

86	    (the degree-`p` term of `sectionCechComplex 𝒰 F`)
87	  Both complexes live in `Ab` after applying the global-sections functor.

90	  For each `p`, the Yoneda/free-presheaf adjunction gives
91	    `Hom(freeYoneda.obj V, F) ≅ F.obj V`  (natural in `V`).

95	  (via `preadditiveYoneda` preservation of limits, or hand-rolled from
96	  `Limits.Sigma.desc` / `Limits.Sigma.ι`), we get a degree-wise `Ab`-iso
97	    `Hom(K(𝒰)_p, F) ≅ ∏_σ F.obj (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) = Č^p(𝒰, F)`.

103	  `Č•(𝒰, F)` is the alternating sum of restriction maps built by `sectionCechComplex`.
104	  These match under the per-degree iso by naturality of `freeYonedaHomAddEquiv`.
105

126

128	`Hom_{PMod}(-, F) = preadditiveYoneda.obj F` to the free Čech simplicial object

149	noncomputable def homCechComplex (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
150	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) : CochainComplex Ab.{u} ℕ :=
151	  (AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex Ab.{u}).obj (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F)

153	/-- **Per-degree component of the Čech hom-identification.**
154	
155	For each simplicial degree `n`, the abelian-group isomorphism
156	`Hom_{PMod}(K(𝒰)_n, F) ≅ ∏_σ F(⨅ₖ U(σ k))` assembled from (i) the coproduct–hom duality
157	`Hom(∐_σ Aσ, F) ≅ ∏_σ Hom(Aσ, F)` (the additive functor `Hom(-, F)` preserves the limit,
158	so `piComparison` is an iso, combined with `opCoproductIsoProduct`), and (ii) the per-index

162	noncomputable def homCechSectionIsoApp (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
163	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (n : SimplexCategory) :
164	    (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F).obj n ≅ (sectionCechCosimplicial (coverOpen 𝒰) F).obj n :=
165	  (preadditiveYoneda.obj F).mapIso
166	      (opCoproductIsoProduct
167	        (fun σ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀ => freeYoneda.obj (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ)))
168	    ≪≫ asIso (piComparison (preadditiveYoneda.obj F)
169	        (fun σ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀ => Opposite.op (freeYoneda.obj (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))))
170	    ≪≫ Limits.Pi.mapIso (fun σ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀ =>
171	        (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) F).toAddCommGrpIso)

173	/-- `Pi.mapIso e` is by definition `Pi.map (fun b => (e b).hom)`. -/
174	private lemma pi_mapIso_hom_eq {β : Type*} {C : Type*} [Category C] {f g : β → C}
175	    [HasProductsOfShape β C] (e : ∀ b, f b ≅ g b) :
176	    (Limits.Pi.mapIso e).hom = Limits.Pi.map (fun b => (e b).hom) := rfl
