178	/-- Characterizing property of `homCechSectionIsoApp`: its `σ`-component is precomposition
179	with the coproduct injection `Sigma.ι σ` followed by the free–Yoneda section identification.
180	Reduces the naturality of the assembled iso to the naturality of `freeYonedaHomAddEquiv`. -/
181	private lemma homCechSectionIsoApp_hom_π (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
182	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (n : SimplexCategory) (σ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) :
183	    (homCechSectionIsoApp 𝒰 F n).hom ≫
184	        Pi.π (fun τ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀ =>
185	          F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (coverInterOpen 𝒰 τ))) σ =
186	      (preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map
187	          (Limits.Sigma.ι (fun τ : Fin (n.len + 1) → 𝒰.I₀ =>
188	            freeYoneda.obj (coverInterOpen 𝒰 τ)) σ).op ≫
189	        (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) F).toAddCommGrpIso.hom := by
190	  rw [homCechSectionIsoApp, Iso.trans_hom, Iso.trans_hom, Functor.mapIso_hom, asIso_hom,
191	    pi_mapIso_hom_eq]
192	  simp only [Category.assoc]
193	  erw [Pi.map_π, piComparison_comp_π_assoc]
194	  rw [← Category.assoc]
195	  congr 1
196	  exact ((preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map_comp _ _).symm.trans
197	    (congrArg _ (opCoproductIsoProduct_hom_comp_π σ))

199	/-- **Naturality of the free–Yoneda section identification in the open.**
200	
201	For an inclusion of opens `h : V ⟶ W`, precomposition with `freeYoneda.map h` on the hom-side
202	corresponds to restriction `F.presheaf.map h.op` on the section side.  This is the single
203	naturality square that powers the cosimplicial naturality of the Čech hom-identification. -/
204	private lemma freeYonedaHomAddEquiv_naturality {V W : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X}
205	    (h : V ⟶ W) (F : X.PresheafOfModules) :
206	    (preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map (freeYoneda.map h).op ≫
207	        (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv V F).toAddCommGrpIso.hom
208	      = (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv W F).toAddCommGrpIso.hom ≫ F.presheaf.map h.op := by
209	  ext ψ
210	  show freeYonedaHomEquiv V F (freeYoneda.map h ≫ ψ)
211	      = (ConcreteCategory.hom (F.presheaf.map h.op)) (freeYonedaHomEquiv W F ψ)
212	  show yonedaEquiv (PresheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv (freeYoneda.map h ≫ ψ))
213	      = (ConcreteCategory.hom (F.presheaf.map h.op))
214	          (yonedaEquiv (PresheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv ψ))
215	  rw [show PresheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv (freeYoneda.map h ≫ ψ)
216	        = yoneda.map h ≫ PresheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv ψ from
217	      (PresheafOfModules.freeAdjunction _).homEquiv_naturality_left (yoneda.map h) ψ,
218	    ← yonedaEquiv_naturality]
219	  rfl

221	/-- **The cosimplicial natural isomorphism `Hom(K(𝒰)_•, F) ≅ Č•(𝒰, F)`.**
222	
223	Assembles the per-degree isomorphisms `homCechSectionIsoApp` into a natural isomorphism of
224	cosimplicial abelian groups. The naturality square reduces, via `homCechSectionIsoApp_hom_π`
225	in both degrees, to the single naturality square `freeYonedaHomAddEquiv_naturality` of the
226	free–Yoneda section identification.

228	Project-local: the cosimplicial comparison of the hom-complex with the section complex has no
229	Mathlib counterpart. -/
230	noncomputable def homCechSectionCosimplicialIso (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
231	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) :
232	    homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F ≅ sectionCechCosimplicial (coverOpen 𝒰) F :=
233	  NatIso.ofComponents (homCechSectionIsoApp 𝒰 F) (by
234	    intro n m f
235	    apply Limits.Pi.hom_ext
236	    intro σ
237	    dsimp only [sectionCechCosimplicial]
238	    rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, Pi.lift_π]
239	    erw [homCechSectionIsoApp_hom_π 𝒰 F m σ]
240	    conv_rhs => rw [← Category.assoc]
241	    erw [homCechSectionIsoApp_hom_π 𝒰 F n (σ ∘ ⇑(SimplexCategory.Hom.toOrderHom f))]
242	    erw [Category.assoc]
243	    erw [← freeYonedaHomAddEquiv_naturality
244	        (homOfLE (coverInterOpen_comp_le 𝒰 ⇑(SimplexCategory.Hom.toOrderHom f) σ)) F]
245	    dsimp only [homCechCosimplicial, Functor.comp_map, Functor.rightOp_map]
246	    erw [← Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]
247	    congr 1
248	    congr 1
249	    apply Quiver.Hom.unop_inj
250	    simp only [unop_comp]
251	    dsimp only [cechFreeSimplicial]
252	    erw [Limits.Sigma.ι_desc]
253	    rfl
254	    )

256	/-- **The Čech hom-identification** (blueprint `lem:cech_complex_hom_identification`).
257	
258	The cochain-complex isomorphism `Hom_{PMod}(K(𝒰)_•, F) ≅ Č•(𝒰, F)` identifying the
259	hom-complex of the free Čech resolution with the section Čech complex of `F`. Obtained by
260	applying the alternating-coface-map complex functor to the cosimplicial natural isomorphism
261	`homCechSectionCosimplicialIso`, so the differential intertwining is automatic from the
262	cosimplicial naturality.

264	Project-local: the comparison of the free-resolution hom-complex with the section complex has
265	no Mathlib counterpart. -/
266	noncomputable def cechComplex_hom_identification (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
267	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) :
268	    homCechComplex 𝒰 F ≅ sectionCechComplex (coverOpen 𝒰) F :=
269	  (AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex Ab.{u}).mapIso (homCechSectionCosimplicialIso 𝒰 F)

271	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — hom-complex as contravariant transport
272	
273	The injective-acyclicity assembly (`lem:injective_cech_acyclic`, gated on Lane-1's
274	`cechFreeComplex_quasiIso`) needs `homCechComplex 𝒰 F` — the alternating *coface* complex of
275	the hom-cosimplicial object `homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F` — to be identified with the
276	contravariant transport `Hom(-, F) = preadditiveYoneda.obj F` of the *opposite* of the free
277	Čech chain complex `cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰`.  Once this identification is in hand,
278	`quasiIso_map_preadditiveYoneda_of_injective` (applied to `(cechFreeComplexAug 𝒰).op`) and
279	`cechComplex_hom_identification` combine in a single step to turn the free resolution into
280	Čech acyclicity of injective sheaves.
281	
282	Project-local: the comparison of the alternating-coface hom-complex with the mapped opposite
283	of the alternating-face free complex has no Mathlib counterpart. -/
284	
285	/-- The `i`-th coface of `homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F` is `Hom(-, F)` applied to the opposite of
286	the `i`-th face of `cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰`.  Holds definitionally (both unfold to
287	`(preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map ((cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).map (SimplexCategory.δ i).op).op`);
288	isolated as a `rfl` lemma to drive the differential identification `homCechComplex_d_eq`. -/
289	private lemma homCechCosimplicial_δ (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
290	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 2)) :
291	    (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F).δ i
292	      = (preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map ((cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).δ i).op :=
293	  rfl
294	
295	/-- **Degreewise differential identification** of the hom-complex with the mapped opposite of
296	the free Čech complex.  Both differentials are alternating sums of (co)faces; pushing the
297	opposite and the additive functor `Hom(-, F)` through the alternating sum on the right and
298	using `homCechCosimplicial_δ` matches them term by term.  This is the naturality input for the
299	cochain-complex isomorphism `homCechComplexMapOpIso`. -/
300	private lemma homCechComplex_d_eq (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
301	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (p : ℕ) :
302	    (homCechComplex 𝒰 F).d p (p + 1)
303	      = (((preadditiveYoneda.obj F).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
304	          (HomologicalComplex.op (cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰))).d p (p + 1) := by
305	  have hL : (homCechComplex 𝒰 F).d p (p + 1)
306	      = AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F) p :=
307	    CochainComplex.of_d (fun n => (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk n)) (AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (homCechCosimplicial 𝒰 F)) p
308	  have hR : (cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰).d (p + 1) p
309	      = AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.objD (cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰) p :=
310	    ChainComplex.of_d (fun n => (cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) (AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.objD (cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰)) p
311	  rw [hL, AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD,
312	    Functor.mapHomologicalComplex_obj_d, HomologicalComplex.op_d, hR,
313	    AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.objD]
314	  have hop := CategoryTheory.op_sum
315	    ((cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (p + 1))))
316	    ((cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk p)))
317	    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (p + 2)))
318	    (fun i => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) • (cechFreeSimplicial 𝒰).δ i)
319	  erw [hop, Functor.map_sum]
320	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
321	  rw [homCechCosimplicial_δ, CategoryTheory.op_zsmul]
322	  erw [Functor.map_zsmul]
323	  rfl

325	/-- **Hom-complex as contravariant transport of the free Čech complex.**
326	
327	The cochain-complex isomorphism `Hom(K(𝒰)_•, F) ≅ Hom(-, F)((K(𝒰)_•)ᵒᵖ)` identifying the
328	alternating-coface hom-complex `homCechComplex 𝒰 F` with the contravariant transport
329	`(preadditiveYoneda.obj F).mapHomologicalComplex` of the opposite of the free Čech chain
330	complex `cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰`.  Degreewise the two complexes have the *same* term
331	(`Hom_{PMod}(K(𝒰)_p, F)`), so the components are identities; the differential squares are
332	`homCechComplex_d_eq`.

334	This is the bridge that turns Lane-1's free resolution into Čech acyclicity: applying
335	`quasiIso_map_preadditiveYoneda_of_injective` to `(cechFreeComplexAug 𝒰).op` produces a
336	quasi-isomorphism of mapped-opposite complexes, and this iso transports it onto
337	`homCechComplex 𝒰 F` (hence, via `cechComplex_hom_identification`, onto `sectionCechComplex`).
338	
339	Project-local: the identification of the alternating-coface hom-complex with the mapped
340	opposite of the alternating-face free complex has no Mathlib counterpart. -/
341	noncomputable def homCechComplexMapOpIso (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
342	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) :
343	    homCechComplex 𝒰 F ≅
344	      ((preadditiveYoneda.obj F).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
345	        (HomologicalComplex.op (cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰)) :=
346	  HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents (fun _ => Iso.refl _) (by
347	    rintro i j (rfl : i + 1 = j)

349	      ((homCechComplex_d_eq 𝒰 F i).symm.trans (Category.comp_id _).symm))

359	across this iso identifies `sectionCechComplex` with the mapped opposite of a complex
360	concentrated in degree `0`, giving positive-degree vanishing.
361	
362	Project-local: assembled from two project-local isomorphisms. -/
363	noncomputable def sectionCechComplexMapOpIso (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
364	    (F : X.PresheafOfModules) :
365	    ((preadditiveYoneda.obj F).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
366	        (HomologicalComplex.op (cechFreePresheafComplex 𝒰))
367	      ≅ sectionCechComplex (coverOpen 𝒰) F :=
368	  (homCechComplexMapOpIso 𝒰 F).symm ≪≫ cechComplex_hom_identification 𝒰 F

370	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — `Hom(-, I)` is exact for injective `I`
371	
372	The presheaf-level Čech-acyclicity argument (`lem:injective_cech_acyclic`) needs the single
373	categorical fact that, for an injective object `I` of an abelian category, the contravariant
374	hom functor `Hom(-, I)` is exact — equivalently, the covariant functor
375	`preadditiveYoneda.obj I : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab` preserves homology. Mathlib supplies the two pieces:
376	`preadditiveYoneda.obj I` always preserves finite limits (it is left exact), and injectivity
377	is equivalent to it preserving epimorphisms; we assemble these into preservation of finite
378	colimits (hence of homology), and feed the result through
379	`HomologicalComplex.quasiIsoAt_map_of_preservesHomology` to obtain quasi-isomorphism
380	preservation. These are stated for a general abelian category so they apply verbatim to
381	`X.PresheafOfModules` once the injectivity of `I` as a presheaf of modules is in hand.
382	
383	Project-local: Mathlib has the ingredients but not the packaged exactness of `Hom(-, I)` as a
384	homology-preserving functor. -/

386	section InjectiveHomExact
387	
388	open CategoryTheory Limits
389	
390	variable {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C]
391	
392	/-- **`Hom(-, I)` preserves finite colimits for injective `I`.** For an injective object `I`
393	of an abelian category, the covariant functor `preadditiveYoneda.obj I : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab`
394	preserves finite colimits: it is left exact (preserves finite limits) automatically, and
395	injectivity makes it preserve epimorphisms, which together with left exactness gives
396	exactness. Combined with the automatic `PreservesFiniteLimits` instance this yields
397	`(preadditiveYoneda.obj I).PreservesHomology` by `Functor.preservesHomologyOfExact`.
398	
399	Project-local: the exactness of `Hom(-, I)` for injective `I` is the categorical engine of
400	`lem:injective_cech_acyclic`. -/
401	instance preadditiveYoneda_obj_preservesFiniteColimits_of_injective
402	    (I : C) [Injective I] : PreservesFiniteColimits (preadditiveYoneda.obj I) := by
403	  have hepi : (preadditiveYoneda.obj I).PreservesEpimorphisms :=
404	    (Injective.injective_iff_preservesEpimorphisms_preadditiveYoneda_obj I).mp inferInstance
405	  rw [Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_epi]
406	  intro S hS
407	  have hg := hS.epi_g
408	  exact ⟨hS.exact.map_of_mono_of_preservesKernel _ hS.mono_f inferInstance,
409	    hepi.preserves S.g⟩
410	
411	/-- **`Hom(-, I)` carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms for injective `I`.**
412	Since `preadditiveYoneda.obj I` preserves homology
413	(`preadditiveYoneda_obj_preservesFiniteColimits_of_injective`), applying it degreewise to a
414	quasi-isomorphism `φ` of chain complexes in `Cᵒᵖ` produces a quasi-isomorphism of the
415	`Hom`-cochain complexes. This is the form consumed by `injective_cech_acyclic`: the
416	augmentation `cechFreeComplexAug 𝒰` (a quasi-isomorphism once Lane 1 lands), taken opposite
417	and mapped through `preadditiveYoneda.obj F`, stays a quasi-isomorphism.
418	
419	Project-local: packages `quasiIsoAt_map_of_preservesHomology` against the injective-hom
420	exactness instance above. -/
421	lemma quasiIso_map_preadditiveYoneda_of_injective (I : C) [Injective I]
422	    {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι} {K L : HomologicalComplex Cᵒᵖ c}
423	    (φ : K ⟶ L) [QuasiIso φ] :
424	    QuasiIso (((preadditiveYoneda.obj I).mapHomologicalComplex c).map φ) := by
425	  rw [quasiIso_iff]
426	  intro i
427	  exact HomologicalComplex.quasiIsoAt_map_of_preservesHomology φ (preadditiveYoneda.obj I) i
428	    (hφ := QuasiIso.quasiIsoAt (f := φ) i)
429	
430	end InjectiveHomExact

432	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — Čech `H¹` vanishing ⟹ cocycles are coboundaries
433	
434	The surjectivity-on-sections step `ses_cech_h1` (blueprint `lem:ses_cech_h1`, Stacks
435	`lemma-ses-cech-h1`) consumes the {\v C}ech-algebra fact that a covering with
436	`Ȟ¹(𝒰, F) = 0` has *every* {\v C}ech `1`-cocycle equal to a coboundary. This is the
437	`\uses{def:cech_complex}` content of that lemma, isolated here as a self-contained
438	statement about the section {\v C}ech complex `sectionCechComplex` (no sheaf gluing or
439	local-surjectivity input). It is the converse direction of
440	`sectionCech_isZero_homology_of_objD_exact` (CechAcyclic), packaged in section

450	/-- **Homology vanishing ⟹ coface-differential exactness** (converse of
451	`sectionCech_isZero_homology_of_objD_exact`). If the degree-`(q+1)` homology of the
452	section {\v C}ech complex vanishes, the underlying group homomorphisms of the two
453	consecutive coface differentials `objD q`, `objD (q+1)` form an exact sequence. Pure
454	homological algebra: the same `exactAt_iff_isZero_homology` / `exactAt_iff'` /
455	`ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact` chain, run in the extraction direction.

457	Project-local: extraction form of the `Ab`-side homology bridge of
458	`lem:section_cech_homology_exact`, needed by the `ses_cech_h1` coboundary step. -/
459	theorem sectionCech_objD_exact_of_isZero_homology {ι : Type u}
460	    (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (q : ℕ)
461	    (h : IsZero ((sectionCechComplex U F).homology (q + 1))) :
462	    Function.Exact
463	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q))
464	      (ConcreteCategory.hom
465	        (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) (q + 1))) := by
466	  have hf : (sectionCechComplex U F).d q (q + 1)
467	      = AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) q :=
468	    CochainComplex.of_d (fun n => (sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk n)) (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F)) q
469	  have hg : (sectionCechComplex U F).d (q + 1) (q + 2)
470	      = AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) (q + 1) :=
471	    CochainComplex.of_d (fun n => (sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk n)) (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F)) (q + 1)
472	  have key : Function.Exact
473	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((sectionCechComplex U F).d q (q + 1)))
474	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((sectionCechComplex U F).d (q + 1) (q + 2))) := by
475	    have hh := h
476	    rw [← HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology,
477	        (sectionCechComplex U F).exactAt_iff' q (q + 1) (q + 2) (by simp) (by simp),
478	        ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at hh
479	    exact hh
480	  rw [hf, hg] at key
481	  exact key
482	
483	/-- **Čech `1`-cocycles are coboundaries when `Ȟ¹(𝒰, F) = 0`** — the
484	`\uses{def:cech_complex}` heart of `ses_cech_h1`.
485	
486	Working in the section coordinates of `sectionCechCosimplicial` (a family of sections
487	`c σ ∈ F(⨅ₖ U (σ k))` indexed by double-indices `σ : Fin 2 → ι`), if the family
488	satisfies the {\v C}ech `1`-cocycle identity (the alternating sum of its restrictions
489	over each triple-index `σ : Fin 3 → ι` vanishes) and the degree-`1` homology of the
490	section {\v C}ech complex vanishes, then `c` is a coboundary: there is a `0`-cochain
491	`t` (sections `t σ ∈ F(U (σ 0))` over single-indices) with `c σ` the alternating sum
492	of the face restrictions of `t`, i.e. `c σ = t_{σ 1}|_{σ} - t_{σ 0}|_{σ}` once the
493	two-term sum is expanded. The restriction maps are `sectionCechFaceRestr`, exactly the
494	{\v C}ech coface restrictions appearing in `sectionCech_objD_apply`.
495	
496	Project-local: the section-coordinate coboundary extraction for the section {\v C}ech
497	complex has no Mathlib counterpart. -/
498	theorem sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology {ι : Type u}
499	    (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules)
500	    (h : IsZero ((sectionCechComplex U F).homology 1))
501	    (c : ∀ σ : Fin 2 → ι, F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))))
502	    (hcoc : ∀ σ : Fin 3 → ι,
503	      ∑ i : Fin 3, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) •
504	        ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U F σ i)
505	          (c (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom)) = 0) :
506	    ∃ t : ∀ σ : Fin 1 → ι, F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))),
507	      ∀ σ : Fin 2 → ι, c σ = ∑ i : Fin 2, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) •
508	        ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U F σ i)
509	          (t (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom)) := by
510	  have he := sectionCech_objD_exact_of_isZero_homology U F 0 h
511	  set c' : ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk 1)) :=
512	    (sectionCechProductEquiv U F 1).symm c with hc'
513	  have hpe1 : sectionCechProductEquiv U F 1 c' = c :=
514	    (sectionCechProductEquiv U F 1).apply_symm_apply c
515	  have hzero : ConcreteCategory.hom
516	      (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U F) 1) c' = 0 := by
517	    apply (sectionCechProductEquiv U F 2).injective
518	    funext σ
519	    rw [sectionCech_objD_apply U F 1 c' σ, hpe1]
520	    rw [show sectionCechProductEquiv U F 2 0 σ = 0 from by
521	      rw [sectionCechProductEquiv_apply]; exact map_zero _]
522	    exact hcoc σ
523	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := (he c').mp hzero
524	  refine ⟨sectionCechProductEquiv U F 0 b, fun σ => ?_⟩
525	  rw [← hpe1, ← hb, sectionCech_objD_apply U F 0 b σ]
526	
527	end CechH1Coboundary

529	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — surjectivity on sections from {\v C}ech-`H¹`
530	vanishing (`ses_cech_h1`)
531	
532	This section assembles the {\v C}ech-`H¹` vanishing into the surjectivity statement
533	`ses_cech_h1` (blueprint `lem:ses_cech_h1`, Stacks `lemma-ses-cech-h1`).  The
534	{\v C}ech-algebra heart is `sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology` (the
535	cocycle-to-coboundary extraction proven above); the remaining content is the standard
536	sheaf theory — local lifting, left-exactness on sections, and gluing — which here is
537	supplied through Mathlib's `TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafUniqueGluing` and a handful of
538	restriction-bookkeeping helpers.
539	
540	Project-local: Mathlib has no {\v C}ech complex of sections of a presheaf of modules, so
541	the surjectivity criterion phrased through `sectionCechComplex` is new here. -/
542	
543	section SesCechH1
544	
545	open AlgebraicTopology TopologicalSpace Opposite
546	
547	/-- **Composite of two presheaf restrictions is the direct restriction.**
548	For `A ≤ B ≤ C` the restriction `P(C) → P(B)` followed by `P(B) → P(A)` equals the direct
549	restriction `P(C) → P(A)`.  Holds definitionally for `Ab`-valued presheaves on opens
550	because the composite of the opposite `homOfLE`s is the opposite `homOfLE` of the
551	composite.  Used pervasively to collapse restriction chains in `ses_cech_h1`. -/
552	private lemma restr_trans (P : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u}) {A B C : Opens ↥X}
553	    (h1 : A ≤ B) (h2 : B ≤ C) (x : ToType (P.obj (op C))) :
554	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h1).op)
555	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h2).op) x)
556	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE (h1.trans h2)).op) x := by
557	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← P.map_comp, ← op_comp]
558	  rfl
559	
560	/-- **Restriction between two equal opens is injective.**  When `V ≤ W` and `W ≤ V`
561	(i.e. `V = W`) the restriction `P(W) → P(V)` is injective: the reverse restriction is a
562	two-sided inverse (`restr_trans` collapses the round trip to the identity, by uniqueness of
563	poset morphisms).  Used to transport the {\v C}ech compatibility equation between the binary
564	intersection `U i ⊓ U j` and the {\v C}ech double-overlap `⨅ₖ U (![i,j] k)`. -/
565	private lemma restr_inj_of_eq (P : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u}) {V W : Opens ↥X}
566	    (h : V ≤ W) (h' : W ≤ V) :
567	    Function.Injective (ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h).op)) := by
568	  intro a b hab
569	  have h2 := congrArg (ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h').op)) hab
570	  rw [restr_trans, restr_trans] at h2
571	  rwa [Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (h'.trans h)) (𝟙 _), op_id, P.map_id,
572	    ConcreteCategory.id_apply, ConcreteCategory.id_apply] at h2
573	
574	/-- **Two parallel restrictions agree.**  Any two restriction maps `P(A) → P(C)` (opposite
575	opens morphisms) act identically, by uniqueness of poset morphisms.  Used to discharge the
576	final defeq-up-to-proof-irrelevance step after collapsing restriction chains with
577	`← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp`. -/
578	private lemma restr_op_unique (P : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u}) {A C : Opens ↥X}
579	    (f g : Opposite.op C ⟶ Opposite.op A) (x : ToType (P.obj (Opposite.op C))) :
580	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map f) x = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map g) x := by
581	  rw [show f = g from Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (Subsingleton.elim _ _)]
582	
583	/-- **Restriction of a single-index {\v C}ech section is invariant under reindexing the
584	tuple.**  For two equal `Fin 1`-tuples `ρ = ρ'` (e.g. `fun _ => i` and `![i,j] ∘ δ`), the
585	restrictions of `g' ρ` and `g' ρ'` to a common open `W` agree.  Proved by `subst` (so the
586	propositional-but-not-definitional tuple equality is discharged without a heterogeneous
587	rewrite), then `restr_op_unique`.  This is the bridge between the `U`-indexed glue family
588	(`fun _ => i`) and the {\v C}ech double-overlap agreement (`![i,j] ∘ δ`). -/
589	private lemma restr_g'_transport {ι : Type u} (U : ι → Opens ↥X) (G : X.PresheafOfModules)
590	    (g' : ∀ ρ : Fin 1 → ι, ToType (G.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (ρ k)))))
591	    {W : Opens ↥X} {ρ ρ' : Fin 1 → ι} (hρ : ρ = ρ')
592	    (f : Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (ρ k)) ⟶ Opposite.op W)
593	    (f' : Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (ρ' k)) ⟶ Opposite.op W) :
594	    ConcreteCategory.hom (G.presheaf.map f) (g' ρ)
595	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (G.presheaf.map f') (g' ρ') := by
596	  subst hρ
597	  exact restr_op_unique G.presheaf f f' (g' ρ)
598	
599	/-- **A morphism of presheaves of modules commutes with the {\v C}ech face restrictions.**
600	For `fι : F.presheaf ⟶ G.presheaf` the section-level map `fι.app` intertwines the
601	{\v C}ech face restriction `sectionCechFaceRestr` of `F` with that of `G`; this is just
602	the naturality of `fι`.  It is the single naturality input that pushes the cocycle and
603	coboundary identities of the heart between `F` and `G`. -/
604	private lemma fι_sectionCechFaceRestr {ι : Type u} (U : ι → Opens ↥X)
605	    (F G : X.PresheafOfModules) (fι : F.presheaf ⟶ G.presheaf)
606	    {q : ℕ} (σ : Fin (q + 2) → ι) (i : Fin (q + 2))
607	    (x : ToType (F.presheaf.obj
608	      (op (⨅ l, U ((σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom) l))))) :
609	    ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U G σ i)
610	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (fι.app _) x)
611	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (fι.app _)
612	          (ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U F σ i) x) := by
613	  unfold sectionCechFaceRestr
614	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, fι.naturality]
615	
616	/-- The single-index {\v C}ech intersection at a constant tuple is the cover member. -/
617	private lemma coverConst_iInf {ι : Type u} (U : ι → Opens ↥X) (i : ι) :
618	    (⨅ k : Fin 1, U ((fun _ => i) k)) = U i := by simp
619	
620	/-- The double-index {\v C}ech intersection at `![i, j]` is the binary intersection. -/
621	private lemma coverPair_iInf {ι : Type u} (U : ι → Opens ↥X) (i j : ι) :
622	    (⨅ k : Fin 2, U (![i, j] k)) = U i ⊓ U j := by
623	  apply le_antisymm
624	  · exact le_inf (iInf_le _ 0) (iInf_le _ 1)
625	  · exact le_iInf (fun k => by fin_cases k <;> simp)
626	
627	/-- The `0`-th face of `![i, j]` is the constant tuple `j`. -/
628	private lemma pair_comp_δ0 {ι : Type u} (i j : ι) :
629	    (![i, j] ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2)).toOrderHom) = (fun _ => j) := by
630	  funext k; fin_cases k; simp [SimplexCategory.δ, Fin.succAbove]
631	
632	/-- The `1`-st face of `![i, j]` is the constant tuple `i`. -/
633	private lemma pair_comp_δ1 {ι : Type u} (i j : ι) :
634	    (![i, j] ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2)).toOrderHom) = (fun _ => i) := by
635	  funext k; fin_cases k; simp [SimplexCategory.δ, Fin.succAbove]
636	
637	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
638	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
639	/-- **Surjectivity on sections from {\v C}ech-`H¹` vanishing** (blueprint `lem:ses_cech_h1`,
640	Stacks `lemma-ses-cech-h1`).
641	
642	For a short exact sequence of presheaves of modules `0 → F → G → H → 0` on a scheme `X`
643	— presented through the underlying `Ab`-presheaf maps `fι`, `gπ`, with `fι` a monomorphism
644	on sections (`hmono`), `gπ ∘ fι = 0` (`hπι`), and every kernel section of `gπ` in the image
645	of `fι` (`hker`) — together with an open cover `U` of the open `⨆ᵢ Uᵢ` such that
646	`Ȟ¹(U, F) = 0` (`hH1`) and a family of local lifts `sLoc i ∈ G(Uᵢ)` of `s ∈ H(⨆ᵢ Uᵢ)`
647	(`hlift`), the section `s` lies in the image of `G(⨆ᵢ Uᵢ) → H(⨆ᵢ Uᵢ)`.
648	
649	The differences `sⱼ|_{ij} − sᵢ|_{ij}` of the local lifts map to `0` in `H`, hence lift to a
650	{\v C}ech `1`-cocycle in `F` (`hker`); the {\v C}ech-`H¹` vanishing makes it a coboundary
651	(`sectionCech_one_coboundary_of_isZero_homology`); subtracting the coboundary makes the
652	corrected lifts agree on overlaps, and the sheaf condition on `G` glues them to a global
653	section of `G` over `⨆ᵢ Uᵢ` mapping to `s` (separatedness of `H` identifies its image with
654	`s`).  The "cofinal system of covers" of the Stacks statement is captured here by taking a
655	single cover satisfying both `Ȟ¹ = 0` and the local-lift property as hypotheses.
656	
657	Project-local: the {\v C}ech surjectivity criterion phrased through `sectionCechComplex` is
658	new here (Mathlib has no {\v C}ech complex of sections of a presheaf of modules). -/
659	theorem ses_cech_h1 {ι : Type u} (U : ι → Opens ↥X)
660	    (F G H : X.PresheafOfModules)
661	    (fι : F.presheaf ⟶ G.presheaf) (gπ : G.presheaf ⟶ H.presheaf)
662	    (hGsh : TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (X := X.toTopCat) G.presheaf)
663	    (hHsh : TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (X := X.toTopCat) H.presheaf)
664	    (hπι : ∀ (V : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ) (x : ToType (F.presheaf.obj V)),
665	      ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app V) (ConcreteCategory.hom (fι.app V) x) = 0)
666	    (hmono : ∀ (V : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ), Function.Injective (ConcreteCategory.hom (fι.app V)))
667	    (hker : ∀ (V : (Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ) (x : ToType (G.presheaf.obj V)),
668	      ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app V) x = 0 → ∃ y, ConcreteCategory.hom (fι.app V) y = x)
669	    (s : ToType (H.presheaf.obj (op (iSup U))))
670	    (hH1 : IsZero ((sectionCechComplex U F).homology 1))
671	    (sLoc : ∀ i, ToType (G.presheaf.obj (op (U i))))
672	    (hlift : ∀ i, ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app (op (U i))) (sLoc i)
673	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (H.presheaf.map (Opens.leSupr U i).op) s) :
674	    ∃ g : ToType (G.presheaf.obj (op (iSup U))),
675	      ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app (op (iSup U))) g = s := by
676	  classical
677	  -- single-index local sections, recast in ⨅-coordinates
678	  set sLoc'coord : (σ : Fin 1 → ι) → ToType (G.presheaf.obj (op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) :=
679	    fun σ => ConcreteCategory.hom (G.presheaf.map (homOfLE (iInf_le _ 0)).op) (sLoc (σ 0))
680	    with hsLoc'coord
681	  set sLoc' : ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U G).obj (SimplexCategory.mk 0)) :=
682	    (sectionCechProductEquiv U G 0).symm sLoc'coord with hsLoc'
683	  have hpe0 : sectionCechProductEquiv U G 0 sLoc' = sLoc'coord :=
684	    (sectionCechProductEquiv U G 0).apply_symm_apply sLoc'coord
685	  -- the degree-1 cochain of G-differences
686	  set cyc1 := ConcreteCategory.hom
687	    (AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD (sectionCechCosimplicial U G) 0) sLoc' with hcyc1
688	  set dGcoord : (σ : Fin 2 → ι) → ToType (G.presheaf.obj (op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) :=
689	    fun σ => sectionCechProductEquiv U G 1 cyc1 σ with hdGcoord
690	  have hdG : ∀ σ : Fin 2 → ι, dGcoord σ
691	      = ∑ i : Fin 2, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) •
692	          ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U G σ i)
693	            (sLoc'coord (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom)) := by
694	    intro σ
695	    have happ := sectionCech_objD_apply U G 0 sLoc' σ
696	    rw [hpe0] at happ
697	    exact happ
698	  -- `gπ` carries a single ⨅-coordinate local section to the restriction of `s`
699	  have hgπsLoc' : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 → ι) (h : (⨅ k, U (ρ k)) ≤ iSup U),
700	      ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app (op (⨅ k, U (ρ k)))) (sLoc'coord ρ)
701	        = ConcreteCategory.hom (H.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op) s := by
702	    intro ρ h
703	    rw [hsLoc'coord, ← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, gπ.naturality,
704	      ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, hlift (ρ 0)]
705	    exact restr_trans H.presheaf (iInf_le _ 0) (le_iSup U (ρ 0)) s
706	  -- `gπ` kills the differences
707	  have hgπdG : ∀ σ : Fin 2 → ι,
708	      ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app (op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) (dGcoord σ) = 0 := by
709	    intro σ
710	    rw [hdG, map_sum]
711	    have key : ∀ i : Fin 2,
712	        ConcreteCategory.hom (gπ.app (op (⨅ k, U (σ k))))
713	          ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) • ConcreteCategory.hom (sectionCechFaceRestr U G σ i)
714	            (sLoc'coord (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom)))
715	        = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) • ConcreteCategory.hom (H.presheaf.map
716	            (homOfLE (le_trans (iInf_le (fun k => U (σ k)) (0 : Fin 2)) (le_iSup U (σ 0)))).op) s := by
717	      intro i
718	      rw [map_zsmul]; congr 1
719	      rw [← fι_sectionCechFaceRestr U G H gπ σ i,
720	        hgπsLoc' (σ ∘ (SimplexCategory.δ i).toOrderHom) (le_trans (iInf_le _ 0) (le_iSup U _))]

11	# Form-B absolute cohomology `H^p(U, F) := Ext^p(jShriekOU U, F)` (P5b input)
12	-/

14	universe u

16	open CategoryTheory Limits CategoryTheory.Abelian
17	
18	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

20	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
21	
22	/-- The standard `HasExt` structure on `X.Modules`, made a section-local instance so the
23	`Ext`-based absolute cohomology below resolves it without the slow `HasSmallLocalizedHom`
24	typeclass search. -/
25	noncomputable local instance hasExtModules : HasExt.{u + 1, u, u + 1} X.Modules :=
26	  HasExt.standard _
27	
28	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — Form-B absolute cohomology -/
29	
30	noncomputable def jShriekOU (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) : X.Modules :=
31	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).obj
32	    ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U))
33	
34	/-- The sheafification adjunction hom-bijection as an `AddEquiv` (additivity holds because
35	the right adjoint is an additive functor and composition is bilinear). -/
36	noncomputable def sheafificationHomAddEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.Modules) :
37	    (jShriekOU U ⟶ F) ≃+
38	      ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U) ⟶
39	        (Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F) :=
40	  { (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).homEquiv
41	      ((PresheafOfModules.free X.ringCatSheaf.obj).obj (yoneda.obj U)) F with
42	    map_add' := by
43	      intro f g
44	      haveI : (SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
45	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).Additive := inferInstance
46	      simp only [Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Adjunction.homEquiv_unit]
47	      erw [Functor.map_add, Preadditive.comp_add]
48	      rfl }
49	
50	noncomputable def jShriekOU_homEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.Modules) :
51	    (jShriekOU U ⟶ F) ≃+
52	      ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op U) :=
53	  (sheafificationHomAddEquiv U F).trans (freeYonedaHomAddEquiv U _)
54	
55	/-- **Form-B absolute cohomology** `H^p(U, F) := Ext^p_{O_X}(jShriekOU U, F)`. -/
56	noncomputable def absoluteCohomology (p : ℕ) (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
57	    (F : X.Modules) : AddCommGrpCat :=
58	  AddCommGrpCat.of (Ext (jShriekOU U) F p)
59	
60	/-- **`H⁰(U, F) ≅ Γ(U, F)`** as abelian groups: degree-zero `Ext` out of the
61	corepresenting object `jShriekOU U` recovers the sections of `F` over `U`. This is the
62	additive corepresentability of global sections specialised to `p = 0`. -/
63	noncomputable def absoluteCohomologyZeroAddEquiv (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
64	    (F : X.Modules) :
65	    Ext (jShriekOU U) F 0 ≃+
66	      ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op U) :=
67	  (AddEquiv.mk' Ext.homEquiv₀ (by
68	    intro a b
69	    refine Ext.homEquiv₀.symm.injective ?_
70	    simp only [Ext.homEquiv₀_symm_apply, Ext.mk₀_add, Ext.mk₀_homEquiv₀_apply])).trans
71	    (jShriekOU_homEquiv U F)
72	
73	/-- **Injective vanishing**: positive-degree absolute cohomology of an injective sheaf of
74	modules vanishes. Direct from `Ext.eq_zero_of_injective` (the injective object is the
75	*second* `Ext` argument, so no restriction of the coefficient sheaf is needed). -/
76	theorem absoluteCohomology_eq_zero_of_injective (n : ℕ) (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
77	    (I : X.Modules) [Injective I] (e : Ext (jShriekOU U) I (n + 1)) : e = 0 :=
78	  Ext.eq_zero_of_injective e
79	
80	/-- **Covariant `H^p(U,-)` long exact sequence, surjectivity at `H^{n₁}(U, F₁)`.**
81	Thin wrapper around `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁` at fixed first argument
82	`jShriekOU U`, for a short exact sequence of `O_X`-modules. -/
83	theorem absoluteCohomology_covariant_exact₁ (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
84	    {S : ShortComplex X.Modules} (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₁ : ℕ}
85	    (x₁ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₁ n₁) (hx₁ : x₁.comp (Ext.mk₀ S.f) (add_zero n₁) = 0)
86	    {n₀ : ℕ} (hn₀ : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
87	    ∃ x₃ : Ext (jShriekOU U) S.X₃ n₀, x₃.comp hS.extClass hn₀ = x₁ :=

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.CechComparisonGate
7	
8	/-!
9	# Gate 4: the Čech-to-derived comparison on 2-affine covers, reduced to affine vanishing
10	
11	This file attacks **gate 4** of the unconditional genus-finiteness consumable
12	`Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`
13	(`CechComparisonGate.lean`), namely the instance
14	
15	```
16	∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily.
17	```
18	
19	`HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` (`MayerVietorisCover.lean`) packages, for the cover `𝒰`, a
20	degreewise `k`-linear comparison
21	`∀ n, cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)` between unnormalised Čech
22	cohomology and the `Ext`-based derived cohomology `HModule'`.
23	
24	## The mathematical reduction (Leray on a 2-affine cover)
25	
26	For the 2-affine cover `S.coverFamily` of a separated `k`-curve `C`, with the three
27	pieces `U₁`, `U₂`, `U₁ ⊓ U₂` affine (the `AffineCoverMVSquare` fields), the comparison
28	is the classical statement "an acyclic cover computes derived cohomology", which for a
29	**two**-element cover is the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence
30	(`HModule'_sequence_exact`, in-tree) fed by **affine Serre vanishing in the constant-`k`
31	sheaf apparatus** `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`, i.e.
32	`Subsingleton (HModule' k (toModuleKSheaf C) i U) = 0` for every affine open `U` and
33	every `i > 0`.  Given that vanishing the comparison assembles degreewise:
34	
35	* `n = 0`: sheaf axiom (`H⁰` on both sides is the group of global sections);
36	* `n = 1`: `AffineCoverMVSquare.cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok` (node N5, in-tree,
37	  unconditional) `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`, chained with the
38	  MV cokernel identification `H1Cok S F ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F 1 ⊤` (which uses the
39	  degree-`0`/degree-`1` slice of the MV LES together with the affine `H¹`-vanishing on
40	  `U₁`, `U₂`);
41	* `n ≥ 2`: both sides vanish — the Čech complex of a 2-element cover is `3`-term, and the
42	  derived side vanishes by the MV LES together with the affine vanishing on
43	  `U₁`, `U₂`, `U₁ ⊓ U₂`.
44	
45	## What this file establishes
46	
47	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_coverFamily` / `isAffineOpen_overlapOpen`: the three
48	  pieces of the cover, in their `coverFamily`/`overlapOpen` typed forms, are affine
49	  (bridging the structure fields to the family-indexed forms the degreewise assembly
50	  consumes).
51	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_coverFamily` /
52	  `subsingleton_hModule'_overlapOpen`: the **per-piece derived vanishing** — under
53	  `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F`, `Subsingleton (HModule' k F i (piece))` for every
54	  `i > 0`.  These are the affine-vanishing inputs the Mayer–Vietoris degreewise assembly
55	  reads off (the `H¹` cokernel identification and the `n ≥ 2` whole-space vanishing are
56	  both immediate consequences of the MV LES fed by exactly these).
57	* `module_finite_hModule_one_unconditional`: the capstone, stated under the honest gate
58	  set (finite map to ℙ¹, ℙ¹ chart data, and the gate-4 comparison), delivering
59	  `Module.Finite k (H¹(C, 𝒪_C))`.  This is `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1`
60	  with the `HasExt` gates synthesised (via `CechComparisonGate`); once the gate-4 instance
61	  is supplied — i.e. once `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` is proved and
62	  the degreewise assembly built — the genus of the curve is honest.
63	
64	## The precise residual
65	
66	The single named residual for the **unconditional** gate 4 is
67	
68	> `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` — affine Serre vanishing
69	> `Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_C) = 0` (`i > 0`, `U` affine) in the `Sheaf (Opens.gT …) (ModuleCat k)`
70	> apparatus —
71	
72	together with the degreewise assembly (the degree-`0`/degree-`1` MV cokernel
73	identification and the `n ≥ 2` whole-space vanishing) built from it.  No `sorry`/axiom or
74	sorried instance is introduced here; the residual is the existing `Prop`-class
75	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing`, whose producer for the structure sheaf is the genuine open
76	target (Mathlib supplies no scheme-cohomology Serre vanishing in this apparatus, and the
77	in-tree `X.Modules` vanishing is gated on the un-instantiable
78	`[EnoughInjectives (Spec R).Modules]`).
79	
80	**Universe note for the assembly (probe-confirmed here).**  The affine vanishing lives at
81	`HModule' = Abelian.Ext.{u}` (`Type u`), but the in-tree Mayer–Vietoris LES
82	`AffineCoverMVSquare.HModule'_sequence` has its `HasExt` baked at `Abelian.Ext.{u+1}`
83	(`Type u+1`): the two carriers are *not* definitionally equal, so the degreewise assembly
84	must transport the per-piece vanishing across the universe bridge
85	`Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` (`MayerVietorisCore.lean`) before feeding it into the LES.
86	This is the same `Ext.{u}` ↔ `Ext.{u+1}` bridge the `HModule'`/`HModule` interface already
87	uses (`HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv`), and is the one non-obvious wrinkle a future
88	author of the assembly must account for.
89	-/
90	
91	set_option autoImplicit false
92	
93	universe u
94	
95	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
96	
97	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
98	
99	section Affineness
100	
101	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
102	
103	/-- Each piece of the 2-element cover family is affine: `S.coverFamily i` is `U₁` or
104	`U₂`, both affine by the `AffineCoverMVSquare` fields. -/
105	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_coverFamily (i : ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) :
106	    IsAffineOpen (S.coverFamily i) := by
107	  rcases i with ⟨i⟩
108	  fin_cases i
109	  · exact S.isAffineOpen_U₁
110	  · exact S.isAffineOpen_U₂
111	
112	/-- The overlap `U₁ ⊓ U₂` of the 2-element cover, in the `overlapOpen` typed form used by
113	the degreewise Čech assembly, is affine. -/
114	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_overlapOpen :
115	    IsAffineOpen S.overlapOpen :=
116	  S.isAffineOpen_inf
117	
118	end Affineness
119	
120	/-! ## Per-piece derived-cohomology vanishing (the acyclicity inputs of the assembly)
121	
122	Under affine Serre vanishing `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F`, each affine piece of the
123	2-affine cover has vanishing higher derived cohomology `HModule'`.  These are the exact
124	inputs the degreewise Čech comparison consumes (the Mayer–Vietoris LES on the cover reads
125	off `H¹(⊤)` and the higher vanishing from precisely these). -/
126	
127	section PieceVanishing
128	
129	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
130	  (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
131	  (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
132	  [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
133	  [IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F]
134	
135	/-- Higher derived cohomology of `F` vanishes on each piece `S.coverFamily j` of the
136	2-affine cover (both pieces are affine). -/
137	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_coverFamily
138	    (j : ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
139	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i (S.coverFamily j)) :=
140	  IsAffineHModuleVanishing.subsingleton_HModule' (F := F) (S.isAffineOpen_coverFamily j) i hi
141	
142	/-- Higher derived cohomology of `F` vanishes on the overlap `U₁ ⊓ U₂` of the 2-affine
143	cover (the overlap is affine). -/
144	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_overlapOpen
145	    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
146	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i S.overlapOpen) :=
147	  IsAffineHModuleVanishing.subsingleton_HModule' (F := F) S.isAffineOpen_overlapOpen i hi
148	
149	end PieceVanishing
150	
151	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
152	
153	/-! ## The capstone: genus finiteness under the honest gate set
154	
155	Once the gate-4 comparison instance
156	`∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily` is available (its unconditional
157	production is the residual `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` plus the
158	degreewise assembly), the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite `k`-module. -/
159	
160	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
161	
162	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
163	
164	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve, honest gate-set form.**  For a curve `C` over `k`
165	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ (`HasFiniteMapToP1`), the ℙ¹ chart data
166	(`P1HasLaurentChartData`), and the Čech-to-derived comparison on 2-affine covers (gate 4),
167	the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a finite `k`-module.
168	
169	This is `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate` (the `HasExt`-free
170	restatement, `CechComparisonGate.lean`) named as the lane capstone.  It becomes
171	**unconditional** exactly when gate 2 (`P1HasLaurentChartData k`, lane A) and gate 4
172	(this file's target instance, whose residual is affine Serre vanishing
173	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`) are both discharged. -/
174	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_unconditional
175	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
176	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
177	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
178	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=
179	  module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate C
180	
181	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

8	/-!
9	# The last genus-finiteness gates: scoping the Čech-to-derived comparison
10	
11	This file scopes the **final** gates of the adelic genus-finiteness consumable
12	`Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1` (`GenusFiniteness.lean`, node `N12`).
13	That consumable is stated under four gates:
14	
15	1. `HasFiniteMapToP1 C`               — node `N9`  (curve ⟶ ℙ¹, in progress elsewhere);
16	2. `P1HasLaurentChartData k`          — node `N11b` (ℙ¹ chart rings, `P1ChartData.lean`);
17	3. `HasExt.{u}` **and** `HasExt.{u+1}` for the sheaf category
18	   `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`
19	   — the ambient `Ext`-theory the `HModule` genus carrier runs on;
20	4. `∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
21	      HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`
22	   — the Čech-to-derived comparison (Leray/Cartan) on 2-affine covers.
23	
24	The question this file answers: **are gates 3 and 4 instantiable today?**
25	
26	## Gate 3 (the `HasExt` pair): INSTANTIABLE — proved here
27	
28	The genus carrier lives in the sheaf category `𝒮 := Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology
29	C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`, i.e. sheaves of `k`-modules for the *constant* base
30	field `k`.  This is the crucial point that dissolves the historical blocker: `𝒮` is a
31	**Grothendieck abelian category** (Mathlib `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} (Sheaf J A)` for a
32	small site `J` and Grothendieck-abelian `A = ModuleCat k`), so Mathlib supplies
33	`EnoughInjectives 𝒮` (`079H`) and both `HasExt.{u} 𝒮`, `HasExt.{u+1} 𝒮` (`HasExt.standard`)
34	**for free**.  See `hasExt_moduleKSheaf` / `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf` /
35	`enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf` / `isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf` below.
36	
37	This is *not* the situation of the `SheafOfModules R = X.Modules` apparatus (`Ext` over the
38	structure sheaf `𝒪_X` as a sheaf of rings), which the historical Čech capstone
39	(`CechToCohomology.cech_eq_cohomology_of_basis`, `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing`)
40	runs on: there Mathlib v4.31 provides *no* Grothendieck-abelian / enough-injectives instance
41	for `SheafOfModules`, so every derived-functor statement in that lane carries
42	`[EnoughInjectives X.Modules]` / `[HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]` as an un-instantiable
43	hypothesis.  The genus carrier deliberately uses the constant-`k` sheaf category precisely to
44	avoid that trap — and the trap is genuinely avoided.
45	
46	Consequence (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): gate 3 can simply be
47	dropped from the `N12` consumable — Mathlib synthesises it — leaving only gates 1, 2, 4.
48	
49	## Gate 4 (the comparison `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso …`): NOT instantiable today
50	
51	`HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` (`MayerVietorisCover.lean`) is the `Prop`-class packaging of the
52	comparison data `∀ n, cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)`, i.e. "for the cover
53	`𝒰`, unnormalised Čech cohomology equals derived (`Ext`) cohomology in every degree".
54	
55	For the 2-affine cover `S.coverFamily` this comparison is *mathematically* the Leray statement
56	"an affine cover is acyclic ⟹ Čech computes cohomology", which for a **two**-element cover is
57	exactly the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence (`HModule'_sequence_exact`, in-tree) together
58	with **affine Serre vanishing in the constant-`k` sheaf apparatus**:
59	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`, i.e. `Subsingleton (HModule' k
60	(toModuleKSheaf C) i U) = 0` for every affine open `U` and every `i > 0`.  Given that vanishing,
61	the comparison assembles degreewise: `n = 0` (sheaf axiom), `n = 1` (`cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok`
62	= node `N5`, in-tree, plus the MV cokernel identification), `n ≥ 2` (both sides vanish).
63	
64	The **precise gap** is therefore this single named input:
65	
66	> **MISSING:** `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` — Serre vanishing
67	> `Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_C) = 0` (`i > 0`, `U` affine) in the `Sheaf (Opens.gT …) (ModuleCat k)` apparatus,
68	> **plus** the degreewise assembly of the 2-cover comparison from it.
69	
70	Neither piece is a one-line consequence of an existing lemma:
71	
72	* Mathlib has no scheme-cohomology Serre vanishing at all, in any apparatus.
73	* The in-tree Serre vanishing `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing` lives in the *wrong*
74	  category (`X.Modules`, `Ext (jShriekOU U)`) and is itself gated on the un-instantiable
75	  `[EnoughInjectives (Spec R).Modules]`; bridging it to the constant-`k` apparatus would need a
76	  "cohomology is independent of the linear structure" comparison that is likewise absent.
77	* The Čech-to-derived carrier `IsAffineHModuleVanishing` is currently *produced* in-tree only
78	  from `HasAffineCechAcyclicCover` — which itself bundles `HasCechToHModuleIso` on the affine
79	  sub-covers, i.e. the very comparison we are trying to instantiate (a circular producer).
80	
81	So gate 4 is a genuine multi-lemma target, **but the historical infrastructure blocker is gone**:
82	because `EnoughInjectives 𝒮` is now available (proved below), the honest way to close gate 4 is
83	to build affine Serre vanishing + the Čech comparison *directly in the constant-`k` sheaf
84	category* `𝒮` (where injective resolutions exist), rather than attempting to route through the
85	blocked `SheafOfModules` lane.  That is the recommended roadmap for the next wave.
86	
87	## Deliverable of this file
88	
89	* the gate-3 infrastructure, proved and named for citation
90	  (`isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf`, `enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf`,
91	  `hasExt_moduleKSheaf`, `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf`);
92	* the gate-3-free restatement of the `N12` consumable
93	  (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): under gates 1, 2, 4 alone,
94	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite `k`-module.  Once `P1ChartData` lands (gate 2) and the gate-4
95	  comparison is built, `Module.Finite k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` — hence the honesty of `genus C` — is
96	  unconditional on a curve with a finite map to ℙ¹.
97	-/

100	
101	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
102	
103	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
104	
105	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

107	/-! ## Gate 3: the `Ext` infrastructure of the constant-`k` sheaf category is present -/
108	
109	/-- The genus-carrier sheaf category `Sheaf (Opens.gT X) (ModuleCat k)` is **Grothendieck
110	abelian**: sheaves valued in the Grothendieck-abelian `ModuleCat.{u} k` on the small site of
111	opens of `X`.  Mathlib's `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} (Sheaf J A)` fires here.  This is the
112	structural fact that makes the derived-functor genus apparatus well-founded (contrast the
113	`SheafOfModules 𝒪_X` apparatus, for which Mathlib v4.31 supplies no such instance). -/
114	theorem isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
115	    IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u}
116	      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
117	  inferInstance

124	    EnoughInjectives
125	      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
126	  inferInstance

131	    HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
132	  inferInstance

135	synthesisable (the ambient `Ext`-theory the universe-bridged `HModule` genus carrier runs on). -/

137	    HasExt.{u+1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=

140	/-! ## Gate-3-free restatement of the genus-finiteness consumable (node `N12`)
141	
142	Because both `HasExt` gates are now synthesised (gate 3 above), the `N12` consumable of
143	`GenusFiniteness.lean` can be restated without them: the only remaining gates are the geometric
144	inputs (`HasFiniteMapToP1 C`, `P1HasLaurentChartData k`) and the Čech-to-derived comparison
145	(gate 4).  This is the honest, tightest current form of adelic genus finiteness. -/
146

8	/-!
9	# Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, the adelic lane's consumable)
10	
11	This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane**.  It composes the two halves
12	of the lane that are now proved:
13	
14	* the **keystone** `Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
15	  (`FinitenessP1.lean`, node `N11`): under the gates `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` and
16	  `P1HasLaurentChartData k`, *some* 2-affine cover `S` of `C` (the pullback of the
17	  standard ℙ¹ charts along the finite map) has finite-dimensional Čech cokernel
18	  `Ȟ¹ = S.H1Cok`, so any comparison `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok` transports the
19	  finiteness to the genus carrier;
20	* the **comparison** `AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok`
21	  (`Cokernel.lean`, nodes `N5` + `N6`): for *every* 2-affine cover `S`, under the
22	  Čech-to-derived gate `HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`,
23	  `HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1 ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok (toModuleKSheaf C)` — the N5 half
24	  (`cechCohomology 1 ≃ₗ H1Cok`) is unconditional, only the N6 half is gated.
25	
26	## The honest gate set
27	
28	The keystone produces an *existential* cover (`D.pullbackSquare π` for a chosen
29	finite `π` and chart data `D`), which cannot be named in a theorem signature; the
30	comparison must therefore be available for **all** 2-affine covers, i.e. the honest
31	Čech-to-derived hypothesis is the `∀`-quantified instance gate
32	`[∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily]` (a `Prop`-class
33	hypothesis with no sorried instance, in the `HasPicScheme`/`HasFiniteMapToP1`
34	gating pattern).  The full gate set of the consumable is
35	
36	* `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` — node `N9`; derived in `FiniteMapToP1.lean` from the single
37	  strictly weaker gate `ExistsNonconstantMapToP1 C` under the ambient curve
38	  hypotheses;
39	* `P1HasLaurentChartData k` — node `N11b`, the ℙ¹ chart-ring computation
40	  (`P1ChartData.lean` is building towards its instance);
41	* `HasExt.{u}`/`HasExt.{u+1}` — the ambient `Ext`-theory instances the `HModule`
42	  machinery runs on;
43	* `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily` — the Čech-to-derived
44	  comparison (Leray/Cartan) for 2-affine covers of the curve.
45	
46	Under these, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a
47	finite-dimensional `k`-vector space, so `genus C = finrank k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is an
48	honest natural number.
49	-/
50	
51	universe u
52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
58	
59	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, gated).**  For a curve `C` over `k`
60	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ and the ℙ¹ chart data, and with the Čech-to-derived
61	comparison available on 2-affine covers, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite
62	`k`-module.  Composes the `N11` keystone `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
63	with the `N5`+`N6` comparison `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok` of `Cokernel.lean`. -/
64	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1
65	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
66	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
67	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
68	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
69	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
70	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=
71	  module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map C
72	    (fun S => ⟨S.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)⟩)
73	
74	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

122	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
123	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
124	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
125	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C) :
126	    HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]

143	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
144	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

316	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`):

342	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
343	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
344	  letI alg2 : Algebra ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
345	               (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
346	    := RingHom.toAlgebra C.hom.appTop.hom
347	  have hM_inter :
348	      Module.Finite ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
349	        (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
350	    rw [← RingHom.finite_algebraMap]; exact hf
351	  refine Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv
352	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
353	    (RingEquiv.refl _) ?_
354	  ext x
355	  simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.refl_apply,
356	    Function.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
357	  have h_kts : (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)).hom =

359	    ext y

362	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ :

368	              congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe h_kts) _
369	    _  = C.hom.appTop.hom x := by

371	        congr 1

373	              (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv).hom x = x
374	        rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]; rfl

494	`IsHModuleHomFinite k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`. Hypotheses `[IsIntegral C.left]`,
495	`[IsProper C.hom]` are class arguments propagated via instance synthesis from
496	the use site (where `C` is concretely a proper integral `Spec k`-scheme, e.g.\ a
497	smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve). -/
498	noncomputable instance instIsHModuleHomFinite_toModuleKSheaf
499	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
500	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :

502	  module_finite_hom := by
503	    haveI := Scheme.module_finite_gammaObj_of_isProper k C
504	    let LE1 := constantSheafGammaHom_linearEquiv k
505	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.of k k)

517	the structure sheaf of a `Spec k`-scheme `C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))`,
518	with respect to an arbitrary indexed family of opens `𝒰 : ι → Opens C.left.toTopCat`.

521	underlying presheaf of `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` (iter-006). The result is a
522	cochain complex valued in `ModuleCat.{u} k`, indexed by `ℕ`.

524	The cohomology of this complex is `Scheme.cechCohomology_OC` below. The
525	downstream comparison theorem (Čech cohomology = derived-functor cohomology
526	= `Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)` for an acyclic cover) is
527	queued for iter-013+; iter-012 only establishes the Čech-side carrier. -/

529	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
530	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) :
531	    CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℕ :=
532	  (cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C))

534	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-012 scaffold): the `n`-th Čech cohomology
535	of the structure sheaf for an arbitrary indexed open cover. Defined as the
536	`n`-th homology of the Čech cochain complex `Scheme.cechCochain_OC`. The
537	result lives in `ModuleCat.{u} k` and therefore carries a `Module k`
538	structure for free; the iter-013+ comparison theorem will identify it
539	with `Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n` when the cover is
540	acyclic. -/
541	noncomputable def Scheme.cechCohomology_OC
542	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
543	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) (n : ℕ) :
544	    ModuleCat.{u} k :=
545	  (Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰).homology n

547	/-- Iter-047: parameterised Čech cochain complex generalising iter-012's
548	`Scheme.cechCochain_OC` to any sheaf of `k`-modules `F`, not just the structure
549	sheaf. Built from the same Mathlib `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`
550	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Cech.lean`) applied to the
551	underlying presheaf of `F`. The result is a cochain complex valued in
552	`ModuleCat.{u} k`, indexed by `ℕ`. Iter-012's specialisation
553	`Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰` is recovered by setting `F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`
554	(see `Scheme.cechCochain_OC_eq` below).
555	
556	This generalisation is the foundational scaffolding the iter-048+ Čech-vs-derived
557	comparison theorem will build on: the comparison map
558	`Scheme.cechCohomology k C F 𝒰 n →ₗ[k] Scheme.HModule' k F n (⨆ᵢ 𝒰 i)`
559	(queued for iter-048) is naturally parameterised over the sheaf `F`, not just
560	the structure sheaf, so the parameterised carrier is the right level of
561	generality. -/
562	noncomputable def Scheme.cechCochain
563	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
564	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
565	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) :
566	    CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℕ :=
567	  (cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F)

569	/-- Iter-047: parameterised Čech cohomology generalising iter-012's
570	`Scheme.cechCohomology_OC`. The `n`-th cohomology of the parameterised Čech
571	cochain complex. The result lives in `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Iter-012's
572	specialisation is recovered by `Scheme.cechCohomology_OC_eq` below. -/
573	noncomputable def Scheme.cechCohomology
574	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
575	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
576	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) (n : ℕ) :
577	    ModuleCat.{u} k :=

580	/-- Iter-047 bridge: iter-012's `Scheme.cechCochain_OC` is definitionally the
581	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` specialisation of `Scheme.cechCochain`. The
582	proof is `rfl` since iter-012's body is the same `(cechComplexFunctor 𝒰).obj
583	((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C))` term. Used by downstream
584	consumers (iter-048+) to switch between the iter-012 structure-sheaf-specific
585	form and the iter-047 parameterised form without semantic loss. -/
586	theorem Scheme.cechCochain_OC_eq
587	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
588	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) :
589	    Scheme.cechCochain_OC C 𝒰 = Scheme.cechCochain C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 :=
590	  rfl

592	/-- Iter-047 bridge: iter-012's `Scheme.cechCohomology_OC` is definitionally the
593	`F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` specialisation of `Scheme.cechCohomology`. -/
594	theorem Scheme.cechCohomology_OC_eq
595	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
596	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) (n : ℕ) :
597	    Scheme.cechCohomology_OC C 𝒰 n =
598	      Scheme.cechCohomology C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n :=
599	  rfl

601	/-- Iter-048: Čech-side acyclicity carrier predicate. The cover `𝒰` is
602	*Čech-acyclic for the sheaf `F` of `k`-modules* on `C` if positive-degree Čech
603	cohomology vanishes (in the `Subsingleton` sense — `Scheme.cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n`
604	has type `ModuleCat.{u} k`, but `Subsingleton` on the underlying type is the
605	natural and more chainable form). Mirrors the iter-040 / iter-043 carrier-
606	predicate pattern: a single-field `Prop` class capturing a combinatorial
607	vanishing condition that downstream consumers receive as an instance argument.
608	
609	This is the foundational Čech-side input that the iter-051 producer instance for
610	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` will consume, in conjunction
611	with the iter-049+ Čech-vs-derived comparison theorem and iter-048's consumer. -/
612	class Scheme.IsCechAcyclicCover
613	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
614	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
615	    {ι : Type u} (𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat) : Prop where
616	  subsingleton_cechCohomology :
617	    ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → Subsingleton (Scheme.cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n)
618	
619	/-- Iter-048: subsingleton transport via Čech acyclicity + comparison.
620	
621	Given the iter-048 carrier hypothesis `[IsCechAcyclicCover F 𝒰]` AND an explicit
622	comparison iso `compIso n : cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰 i)`
623	(the Čech-vs-derived comparison, queued for iter-049+ to construct as a
624	theorem), conclude that `Subsingleton (HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰 i))` for `n ≥ 1`.
625	
626	The `compIso` is taken as an *explicit argument*, not a class field. The
627	comparison itself is a `LinearEquiv` (data), so it cannot be a field of a
628	`Prop`-valued class; more importantly, decoupling the Čech-side combinatorial
629	vanishing (iter-048) from the substantive comparison theorem (iter-049+) lets
630	each step land as a single iteration. Iter-049+ will provide the comparison as
631	a theorem, which iter-048's consumer accepts directly via this argument.
632	
633	The consumer body extracts the class field (the `Subsingleton` on
634	`cechCohomology n`) and transports along `(compIso n).symm.toEquiv.subsingleton`. -/
635	theorem Scheme.subsingleton_HModule'_supr_of_isCechAcyclicCover
636	    {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
637	    {F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)}
638	    {ι : Type u} {𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat}
639	    [Scheme.IsCechAcyclicCover F 𝒰]
640	    (compIso : ∀ (n : ℕ),
641	      Scheme.cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k]
642	        Scheme.HModule' k F n (⨆ i, 𝒰 i))
643	    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
644	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F n (⨆ i, 𝒰 i)) := by
645	  haveI := Scheme.IsCechAcyclicCover.subsingleton_cechCohomology
646	    (F := F) (𝒰 := 𝒰) n hn
647	  exact (compIso n).symm.toEquiv.subsingleton
648	
649	/-- Iter-048: curve specialisation at `F := Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C`.
650	
651	Mirrors the iter-039 / iter-042 / iter-043 `_curve` pattern: a thin dot-notation
652	wrapper that saves call sites in the curve setting (where `F` is the structure
653	sheaf) from re-typing `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C` whenever the iter-048 consumer
654	is chained through. Used by the iter-051 `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`
655	producer instance. -/
656	theorem Scheme.subsingleton_HModule'_supr_of_isCechAcyclicCover_curve
657	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
658	    {ι : Type u} {𝒰 : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat}
659	    [Scheme.IsCechAcyclicCover (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰]
660	    (compIso : ∀ (n : ℕ),
661	      Scheme.cechCohomology C (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k]
662	        Scheme.HModule' k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n (⨆ i, 𝒰 i))
663	    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
664	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) n (⨆ i, 𝒰 i)) :=
665	  Scheme.subsingleton_HModule'_supr_of_isCechAcyclicCover (𝒰 := 𝒰) compIso n hn
666

32	/-- Iter-046 (Mathlib gap-fill): `Functor.const C : D ⥤ C ⥤ D` is additive when `D`
33	is preadditive. The `map_add` field reduces to `f + g = f + g` componentwise after
34	`ext; rfl`. -/
35	instance Functor.const_additive {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u₂}
36	    [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] : (Functor.const C : D ⥤ C ⥤ D).Additive where
37	  map_add := by intros; ext; rfl
38	
39	/-- Iter-046 (Mathlib gap-fill): `Functor.const C : D ⥤ C ⥤ D` is `R`-linear when
40	`D` is `Linear R`-enriched. The `[CategoryTheory.Linear R D]` qualification is
41	load-bearing — bare `[Linear R D]` would be parsed as `Linear` of a functor. -/
42	instance Functor.const_linear {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u₂}
43	    [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] (R : Type*) [Semiring R]
44	    [CategoryTheory.Linear R D] :
45	    (Functor.const C : D ⥤ C ⥤ D).Linear R where
46	  map_smul := by intros; ext; rfl
47	
48	namespace Adjunction
49	
50	variable {C₁ : Type u} {D₁ : Type u₂} [Category.{v} C₁] [Category.{v₂} D₁]
51	    [Preadditive C₁] [Preadditive D₁] {F : C₁ ⥤ D₁} {G : D₁ ⥤ C₁} (adj : F ⊣ G)
52	    (R : Type*) [Semiring R] [CategoryTheory.Linear R C₁] [CategoryTheory.Linear R D₁]
53	
54	include adj
55	
56	/-- Iter-046 (Mathlib gap-fill): if `G : D ⥤ C` is `R`-linear and `adj : F ⊣ G`,
57	then `F : C ⥤ D` is `R`-linear. Mirrors Mathlib's `left_adjoint_additive`; the
58	`simp` call closes via unit naturality + the `Linear.smul_comp` / `Linear.comp_smul`
59	default simp lemmas. -/
60	lemma left_adjoint_linear [G.Additive] [G.Linear R] : F.Linear R where
61	  map_smul {X Y} f r := (adj.homEquiv _ _).injective (by
62	    -- v4.31.0: the old `simp [adj.homEquiv_unit]` no longer closes; the categorical
63	    -- `Linear.comp_smul`/`smul_comp` only match via `erw` (the `≃ₗ` homModule smul is defeq but
64	    -- not syntactically the `Linear.smul` instance), with unit-naturality in between.
65	    simp only [adj.homEquiv_unit, Functor.map_smul, ← Functor.comp_map]
66	    erw [← adj.unit.naturality, Linear.comp_smul, ← adj.unit.naturality, Linear.smul_comp]
67	    rfl)
68	
69	/-- Iter-046 (Mathlib gap-fill): if `F : C ⥤ D` is `R`-linear and `adj : F ⊣ G`,
70	then `G : D ⥤ C` is `R`-linear. The dual of `left_adjoint_linear`. -/
71	lemma right_adjoint_linear [F.Additive] [F.Linear R] : G.Linear R where
72	  map_smul {X Y} f r := (adj.homEquiv _ _).symm.injective (by
73	    simp [adj.homEquiv_counit])
74	
75	/-- Iter-046 (Mathlib gap-fill): linear lifting of `Adjunction.homAddEquiv`. Under
76	`[F.Additive] [G.Additive] [G.Linear R]`, the additive equivalence
77	`(F.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃+ (X ⟶ G.obj Y)` upgrades to a `LinearEquiv` over `R`. The
78	`change` is load-bearing: it exposes the underlying `homEquiv` form, allowing
79	`simp [homEquiv_unit]` to close via the same naturality argument as in
80	`left_adjoint_linear`. -/
81	noncomputable def homLinearEquiv [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [G.Linear R]
82	    (X : C₁) (Y : D₁) : (F.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ G.obj Y) :=
83	  haveI : F.Linear R := adj.left_adjoint_linear R
84	  { adj.homAddEquiv X Y with
85	    map_smul' := fun r f => by
86	      change adj.homEquiv _ _ (r • f) = r • adj.homEquiv _ _ f
87	      simp only [adj.homEquiv_unit, Functor.map_smul]
88	      erw [Linear.comp_smul] }
89	
90	end Adjunction

123	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (1): the ring map `k → Γ(C, U)` induced by the
124	structure morphism `C.hom : C.left ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)` and the
125	restriction along `U ≤ ⊤`. -/
126	noncomputable def kToSection (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
127	    (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ) :
128	    (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ C.left.presheaf.obj U :=
129	  (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫
130	    C.hom.app ⊤ ≫ C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top).op
131	
132	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (2): `Γ(C, U)` is a `k`-algebra via the ring
133	map of `kToSection`. -/
134	noncomputable instance algebraSection (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
135	    (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ) :
136	    Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.obj U) :=
137	  RingHom.toAlgebra (kToSection C U).hom
138	
139	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (3): unfolding lemma for the algebra map. -/
140	lemma algebraMap_eq_kToSection (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
141	    (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ) :
142	    (algebraMap k (C.left.presheaf.obj U)) = (kToSection C U).hom :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (4): the structure-morphism algebra map is
146	natural in `U`. -/
147	lemma kToSection_naturality (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
148	    {U V : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) :
149	    kToSection C U ≫ C.left.presheaf.map f = kToSection C V := by
150	  simp only [kToSection, Category.assoc, ← C.left.presheaf.map_comp]
151	  rfl
152	
153	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (5): corollary of (4) at the level of
154	`algebraMap`. -/
155	lemma algebraMap_naturality (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
156	    {U V : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V) (r : k) :
157	    (C.left.presheaf.map f).hom (algebraMap k (C.left.presheaf.obj U) r)
158	      = algebraMap k (C.left.presheaf.obj V) r := by
159	  rw [algebraMap_eq_kToSection, algebraMap_eq_kToSection]
160	  exact congrArg (fun (g : (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ _) => g.hom r)
161	    (kToSection_naturality (C := C) f)

169	/-- Phase A step 5 main, helper (6): the presheaf of `k`-modules built from
170	`O_C` and the structure-morphism algebra structure. -/
171	noncomputable def toModuleKPresheaf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
172	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
173	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k (C.left.presheaf.obj U)
174	  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
175	    { toFun := fun x => (C.left.presheaf.map f).hom x
176	      map_add' := fun x y => by
177	        simp [(C.left.presheaf.map f).hom.map_add]
178	      map_smul' := fun r x => by
179	        simp only [Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.map_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
180	        congr 1
181	        exact AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality
182	          (C := C) f r }
183	  map_id U := by
184	    ext x
185	    simp only [ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
186	      ModuleCat.hom_id, LinearMap.id_coe, id_eq]
187	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_id U)) x
188	  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
189	    ext x
190	    simp only [ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
191	      ModuleCat.hom_comp, LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
192	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x
193	
194	/-- Object-evaluation simp lemma for `toModuleKPresheaf`. Definitionally true
195	by construction; tagged `@[simp]` so consumers can rewrite without unfolding
196	the constructor. Phase A step 5 polish (iter-007). -/
197	@[simp] lemma toModuleKPresheaf_obj (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
198	    (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)ᵒᵖ) :
199	    (toModuleKPresheaf C).obj U = ModuleCat.of k (C.left.presheaf.obj U) :=

32	lemma toModuleKPresheaf_isSheaf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
33	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat)
34	      (toModuleKPresheaf C) := by
35	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _ (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
36	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
37	      (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u})).mp C.left.sheaf.property using 1 <;> rfl

40	of `k`-modules. Bundles `toModuleKPresheaf` (helper 6) and
41	`toModuleKPresheaf_isSheaf` (helper 7) into the standard `Sheaf` shape. -/
42	noncomputable def toModuleKSheaf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
43	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=
44	  ⟨toModuleKPresheaf C, toModuleKPresheaf_isSheaf C⟩

51	`Iso.refl _`; probe-confirmed (`lean_run_code`, iter-007 plan-agent). -/
52	noncomputable def toModuleKSheaf_forgetCompare
53	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
54	    (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat)
55	        (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} k) AddCommGrpCat.{u})).obj (toModuleKSheaf C)
56	      ≅ toAbSheaf C.left :=
